title.zh: 卷二 魏書二 文帝紀
title.en: Volume 2: Book of Wei 2 - Annals of Emperor Wen
title.raw: 卷二 魏書二 文帝紀 Volume 2: Book of Wei 2 - Annals of Emperor Wen

sentences.zh: 文皇帝諱丕，字子桓，武帝太子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen, taboo name Pi, courtesy name Zihuan, was the heir son of Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen—whose personal name was Pi and courtesy name Zihuan—was the heir apparent of Emperor Wu (Cao Cao).

sentences.zh: 中平四年冬，生于譙。

translations.literal: In the winter of the fourth year of Zhongping, he was born in Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was born at Qiao in the winter of the fourth year of the Zhongping era (187 CE).

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：帝生時，有雲氣青色而圜如車盖當其上，終日，望氣者以爲至貴之證，非人臣之氣。

translations.literal: The Wei Book says: When the Emperor was born, there was green cloud vapor, round like a carriage canopy, suspended above him all day; those who read auspicious vapors took it as proof of the utmost nobility, not the aura of a mere subject.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book records that at his birth a greenish aura hung above him in a disk like a carriage canopy for the whole day; diviners of qi pronounced it the sign of supreme eminence—not the kind of portent that attends an ordinary minister.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，能屬文。

translations.literal: At age eight, he could compose connected literary pieces.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he could already write polished compositions.

sentences.zh: 有逸才，遂博貫古今經傳諸子百家之書。

translations.literal: He had outstanding talent, and thereupon broadly mastered the classics and commentaries and the writings of the hundred schools from ancient to modern times.
translations.idiomatic: Gifted with extraordinary ability, he went on to command the classics and their commentaries and the writings of the hundred schools past and present.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，好擊劔。

translations.literal: He was skilled at riding and archery, and fond of fencing.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at horsemanship and archery and delighted in swordplay.

sentences.zh: 舉茂才，不行。

translations.literal: He was recommended as a maocai (flourishing talent), but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Nominated as a "flourishing talent," he declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 《獻帝起居注》曰：建安十五年，爲司徒趙溫所辟。

translations.literal: The Daily Records of Emperor Xian says: In the fifteenth year of Jian'an, he was summoned by Minister of Education Zhao Wen.
translations.idiomatic: According to the Daily Records of Emperor Xian, in Jian'an 15 (210 CE) he was recruited by Minister of Education Zhao Wen.

sentences.zh: 太祖表「溫辟臣子弟，選舉故不以實」。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor memorialized: "Zhao Wen has summoned my sons and younger relatives; therefore the selection is not according to reality."
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao submitted a memorial charging that Zhao Wen had recruited his sons and nephews, so the nomination was not based on genuine merit.

sentences.zh: 使侍中守光祿勳郗慮持節奉策免溫官。〉

translations.literal: He ordered Palace Attendant acting Supervisor of the Household Xi Lu, bearing the insignia, to present the edict and dismiss Zhao Wen from office.
translations.idiomatic: He had Palace Attendant and acting Supervisor of the Household Xi Lu carry the credential and deliver the edict stripping Zhao Wen of his post.

sentences.zh: 建安十六年，爲五官中郎將、副丞相。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Jian'an, he became General of the Household for All Purposes and deputy to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In Jian'an 16 (211 CE) he was appointed General of the Household for All Purposes and deputy to the Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，立爲魏太子。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was established as heir apparent of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year of Jian'an (217 CE) he was named heir apparent of Wei.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：太祖不時立太子，太子自疑。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary says: The Grand Progenitor did not promptly establish an heir apparent; the heir apparent himself grew doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary notes that Cao Cao had long delayed naming an heir, and the crown prince began to doubt his position.

sentences.zh: 是時有高元呂者，善相人，乃呼問之，對曰：「其貴乃不可言。

translations.literal: At this time there was a man named Gao Yuanlü who was skilled at physiognomy; he was summoned and asked, and replied: "His nobility cannot be described in words.
translations.idiomatic: There was a physiognomist named Gao Yuanlü whom Pi summoned and questioned; Gao answered, "The degree of eminence is beyond words."

sentences.zh: 」問：「壽幾何？

translations.literal: " He was asked: "How long will his lifespan be?
translations.idiomatic: Pi asked, "How long will he live?"

sentences.zh: 」元呂曰：「其壽，至四十當有小苦，過是無憂也。

translations.literal: " Yuanlü said: "As for his lifespan, when he reaches forty there will be a small hardship; beyond that there will be no worries.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yuanlü replied, "He will meet a brief ordeal at forty; after that, nothing to fear."

sentences.zh: 」後無幾而立爲王太子，至年四十而薨。〉

translations.literal: " Not long afterward he was established as heir apparent of the king; he reached age forty and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Pi was installed as heir apparent of the King of Wei; he died in his fortieth year."

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，嗣位爲丞相、魏王。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor died; he succeeded to the posts of Chancellor and King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao died, Pi succeeded him as Chancellor and King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 〈袁宏《漢紀》載漢帝詔曰：「魏太子丕：昔皇天授乃顯考以翼我皇家，遂攘除羣凶，拓定九州，弘功茂績，光于宇宙，朕用垂拱負扆二十有餘載。

translations.literal: Yuan Hong's Han Annals carries an edict of the Han Emperor: "Wei heir apparent Pi: Formerly August Heaven entrusted your illustrious father to aid Our royal house; thereupon he swept away the multitude of villains and expanded and settled the Nine Provinces; his grand merit and abundant deeds shine through the universe; I therefore leaned on the rail with folded arms for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hong's Han Annals preserves an imperial edict: "Heir apparent Pi of Wei: High Heaven once entrusted your late father to uphold Our house; he crushed the rebels, pacified the Nine Regions, and left achievements that fill heaven and earth—while I, leaning on the cushions at court, reigned at ease for more than twenty years."

sentences.zh: 天不憖遺一老，永保余一人，早世潛神，哀悼傷切。

translations.literal: Heaven is not willing to leave Us one elder to forever protect Us alone; he departed the world early and concealed his spirit; Our grief and mourning are cutting.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven would not spare one wise elder to shelter Me alone; he left the world too soon, and My sorrow cuts deep."

sentences.zh: 丕奕世宣明，宜秉文武，紹熙前緒。

translations.literal: Pi in successive generations shines brightly; he should grasp civil and military affairs and continue and brighten the former threads.
translations.idiomatic: Pi carries forward a luminous succession; he should wield both civil and military authority and carry on the work begun before him."

sentences.zh: 今使使持節御史大夫華歆奉策詔授丕丞相印綬、魏王璽紱，領冀州牧。

translations.literal: Now sending Bearer of the Imperial Insignia Imperial Counselor Hua Xin to present by edict and confer on Pi the Chancellor's seal-cord, the King of Wei's seal and ribbon, and headship as Governor of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore dispatch Bearer of the Imperial Insignia and Imperial Counselor Hua Xin to deliver the edict investing Pi with the Chancellor's seal and ribbon, the regalia of the King of Wei, and the governorship of Ji Province."

sentences.zh: 方今外有遺虜，遐夷未賔，旗鼓猶在邊境，干戈不得韜刃，斯乃播揚洪烈，立功垂名之秋也。

translations.literal: At present beyond Us there remain remnant barbarians; distant tribes have not yet submitted; banners and drums are still at the borders; weapons cannot sheath their blades—this is indeed the autumn season for spreading abroad mighty deeds and establishing merit to leave a name.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians still linger beyond the frontiers, distant peoples have not yet come to court, signal drums stand posted along the borders, and arms cannot yet be laid aside—this is the very hour to broadcast great deeds and win lasting fame."

sentences.zh: 豈得脩諒闇之禮，究曾、閔之志哉？

translations.literal: How can one observe the rites of silent mourning in the dark chamber and exhaust the intentions of Zeng and Min?
translations.idiomatic: How could you confine yourself to solitary mourning like a common heir or imitate only the filial retreats of Zengzi and Min Ziqian?"

sentences.zh: 其敬服朕命，抑弭憂懷，旁祗厥緒，時亮庶功，以稱朕意。

translations.literal: Respectfully obey Our command; suppress and extinguish anxious thoughts; broadly reverence its continuation; seasonally brighten the various achievements, thereby matching Our intention.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore obey this charge with reverence: set anxiety aside, uphold the legacy on every side, and in due course bring every task to fruition, that My wishes may be fulfilled."

sentences.zh: 於戲，可不勉與！」〉

translations.literal: Alas, can you not exert yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Ah—how could you do otherwise than strive with all your might!"

sentences.zh: 尊王后曰王太后。

translations.literal: The queen consort was honored as Queen Dowager of the King.
translations.idiomatic: The queen consort was elevated to Queen Dowager of Wei.

sentences.zh: 改建安二十五年爲延康元年。

translations.literal: He changed the twenty-fifth year of Jian'an to be the first year of Yan Kang.
translations.idiomatic: The twenty-fifth year of Jian'an was redesignated the first year of the Yan Kang era (220 CE).

sentences.zh: 元年二月

translations.literal: Second month of the first year.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the first year of Yan Kang.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載庚戌令曰：「關津所以通商旅，池苑所以御災荒也。

translations.literal: The Wei Book records a Gengxu edict: "Passes and fords exist to facilitate merchants and travelers; ponds and parks exist to cope with famine and disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book preserves an edict issued on the gengxu day: "Barrier crossings exist to keep trade flowing; imperial ponds and preserves exist to buffer times of famine."

sentences.zh: 設禁重稅，非所以便民；

translations.literal: To establish prohibitions and heavy taxes is not the means to benefit the people;
translations.idiomatic: Heavy taxes and strict closure are no way to serve the people;"

sentences.zh: 其除池籞之禁，輕關津之稅，皆復什一。

translations.literal: remove the prohibitions on pond preserves, lighten the taxes on passes and fords, and in all cases return to a one-tenth levy.
translations.idiomatic: therefore lift the embargoes on the royal fisheries, ease duties at the fords, and restore the ten-percent rate everywhere."

sentences.zh: 」辛亥，賜諸侯王將相已下大將粟萬斛，帛千匹，金銀各有差等。

translations.literal: " On Xinhai, he bestowed on the kings of the feudal states, generals, and ministers down to great generals ten thousand hu of grain, a thousand bolts of silk, and gold and silver in graduated amounts.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day that followed, he granted the royal princes, the high ministers, and the senior generals ten thousand hu of grain, a thousand rolls of silk, and graded gifts of gold and silver."

sentences.zh: 遣使者循行郡國，有違理掊克暴虐者，舉其罪。〉

translations.literal: He dispatched envoys to tour the commanderies and kingdoms; where there were those who violated principle, extorted, or were cruel and violent, he reported their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He sent inspectors through the commanderies and principalities to report any official who defied law, extorted the people, or ruled with cruelty."

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以大中大夫賈詡爲太尉，御史大夫華歆爲相國，大理王朗爲御史大夫。

translations.literal: On Renxu, he appointed Grand Counselor Jia Xu as Grand Commandant, Imperial Counselor Hua Xin as Chancellor of State, and Court Administrator Wang Lang as Imperial Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day he named Grand Counselor Jia Xu Grand Commandant, Imperial Counselor Hua Xin Chancellor of State, and Court Administrator Wang Lang Imperial Counselor.

sentences.zh: 置散騎常侍、侍郎各四人，其宦人爲官者不得過諸署令；

translations.literal: He established four Regular Palace Gentlemen and four Gentlemen of the Household each; those eunuchs who served as officials could not exceed the rank of directors of the various offices;
translations.idiomatic: He created four posts each of Regular Palace Gentlemen and Gentlemen Attendant at the Household; no eunuch in office might rise above the rank of director of a bureau;"

sentences.zh: 爲金策著令，藏之石室。

translations.literal: he made a golden tally recording the ordinance and stored it in the stone chamber.
translations.idiomatic: the rule was inscribed on a golden tablet and deposited in the stone archive."

sentences.zh: 初，漢熹平五年，黃龍見譙，光祿大夫橋玄問太史令單颺：「此何祥也？

translations.literal: Formerly, in the fifth year of Han Xiping, a yellow dragon appeared at Qiao; Grand Counselor of the Household Qiao Xuan asked the Grand Astrologer Shan Yang: "What kind of auspice is this?
translations.idiomatic: Long ago, in the fifth year of the Xiping era (176 CE), a yellow dragon was sighted at Qiao. Grand Counselor of the Household Qiao Xuan asked Grand Astrologer Shan Yang what omen it foretold.

sentences.zh: 」颺曰：「其國後當有王者興，不及五十年，亦當復見。

translations.literal: " Yang said: "Afterwards in this state a king will arise; before fifty years have passed, it should also appear again.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Yang answered, "This land will one day produce a true king; within fifty years the dragon should appear again."

sentences.zh: 天事恒象，此其應也。

translations.literal: Affairs of Heaven constantly take symbolic form; this is its correspondence.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's workings always leave images on earth—this was its sign."

sentences.zh: 」內黃殷登默而記之。

translations.literal: " Yin Deng of Neihuang silently recorded it.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Deng of Neihuang quietly committed the prophecy to memory."

sentences.zh: 至四十五年，登尚在。

translations.literal: When forty-five years had passed, Deng was still alive.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-five years later Yin Deng was still living.

sentences.zh: 三月，黃龍見譙，登聞之曰：「單颺之言，其驗茲乎！」

translations.literal: In the third month, a yellow dragon appeared at Qiao; Deng heard of it and said: "Shan Yang's words—are they verified in this!
translations.idiomatic: In the third month another yellow dragon appeared at Qiao; when Yin Deng heard the news he declared, "So Shan Yang's prediction has come true after all!"

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：王召見登，謂之曰：「昔成風聞楚丘之繇而敬事季友，鄧晨信少公之言而自納光武。

translations.literal: The Wei Book says: The King summoned Deng and said to him: "Formerly Cheng Feng heard the oracle of Qiu of Chu and respectfully served Ji You; Deng Chen believed Shaogong's words and himself joined Guangwu.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book relates that the King summoned Yin Deng and told him, "Long ago Lady Cheng Feng heeded the oracle of Chuqiu and honored Ji You; Deng Chen trusted Shaogong's prophecy and threw in his lot with Guangwu."

sentences.zh: 登以篤老，服膺占術，記識天道，豈有是乎！

translations.literal: Deng, by extreme old age, embraced divination arts in his breast, recorded and knew the Way of Heaven—could there be truth in this!
translations.idiomatic: You are aged yet devoted to astrology and what Heaven records—could there be substance to what you heard?"

sentences.zh: 」賜登穀二百斛，遣歸家。〉

translations.literal: " He bestowed on Deng two hundred hu of grain and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: He awarded Yin Deng two hundred hu of grain and sent him home."

sentences.zh: 已卯，以前將軍夏侯惇爲大將軍。

translations.literal: On Jimao, he appointed Former General Xiahou Dun as Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: On the jimao day he promoted Former General Xiahou Dun to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 濊貃、扶餘單于、焉耆、于闐王皆各遣使奉獻。

translations.literal: The Huimo, the Chanyu of Fuyu, Yanqi, and the king of Yutian each dispatched envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu tribes, the king of Fuyu, Yanqi, and the ruler of Yutian each sent envoys with tribute offerings.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：丙戌，令史官奏修重、黎、羲、和之職，欽若昊天，歷象日月星辰以奉天時。

translations.literal: The Wei Book says: On Bingxu, he ordered the historiographers to memorialize on restoring the offices of Chong, Li, Xi, and He, reverently conforming to vast Heaven, calculating and imaging sun, moon, and stars to obey heavenly seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book notes that on the bingxu day he instructed the court historians to revive the offices of Chong, Li, Xi, and He—those who once regulated the calendar—and align celestial observations with the seasons.

sentences.zh: 臣松之案：《魏書》有是言而不聞其職也。

translations.literal: Your subject Song Zhi notes: The Wei Book has this statement but one does not hear of their offices.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi remarks: The Wei Book mentions this reform but gives no details of the offices established.

sentences.zh: 丁亥令曰：「故尚書僕射毛玠、奉常王脩、涼茂、郎中令袁渙、少府謝奐、萬潛、中尉徐奕、國淵等，皆忠直在朝，履蹈仁義，並早即世，而子孫陵遲，惻然愍之，其皆拜子男爲郎中。」〉

translations.literal: A Dinghai edict said: "The late Supervisor of the Secretariat Mao Jie, Chamberlain for Ceremonials Wang Xiu, Liang Mao, Prefect of the Gentlemen of the Household Yuan Huan, Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues Xie Huan, Wan Qian, Commandant of the Capital Guards Xu Yi, Guo Yuan, and others—all were loyal and upright at court, treading in benevolence and righteousness; alike they departed the world early, while their sons and grandsons declined; moved with pity I mourn them—let their sons all be appointed Gentlemen of the Household."
translations.idiomatic: An edict issued on the dinghai day declared: "Former Deputy Director Mao Jie, Chamberlain for Ceremonials Wang Xiu, Liang Mao, Prefect of the Household Yuan Huan, Chamberlain Xie Huan and Wan Qian, Capital Commandant Xu Yi, Guo Yuan, and the rest served with upright loyalty and walked the path of humanity and justice, yet died young while their families fell into hardship. Out of compassion I hereby appoint each man's heir as a Gentleman of the Household."

sentences.zh: 夏四月丁巳，饒安縣言白雉見。

translations.literal: In summer, fourth month, on Dingsi, Rao'an County reported that a white pheasant appeared.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer, on the dingsi day, Rao'an County reported the sighting of a white pheasant.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：賜饒安田租，勃海郡百戶牛酒，大酺三日；

translations.literal: The Wei Book says: He granted Rao'an exemption from field rent, to Bohai commandery a hundred households' oxen and wine, and great festive drinking for three days;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book adds that he remitted land tax for Rao'an, sent cattle and wine to a hundred households in Bohai for a three-day general feast;

sentences.zh: 太常以太牢祠宗廟。〉

translations.literal: the Chamberlain for Ceremonials sacrificed the grand beast at the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: and had the Chamberlain for Ceremonials offer the grand sacrifice at the ancestral shrine."

sentences.zh: 庚午，大將軍夏侯惇薨。

translations.literal: On Gengwu, Grand General Xiahou Dun died.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day Grand General Xiahou Dun died.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：王素服幸鄴東城門發哀。

translations.literal: The Wei Book says: The King in plain dress proceeded to the eastern gate of Ye to express grief.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book records that the King, dressed in mourning white, went to the east gate of Ye to mourn.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：在禮，天子哭同姓於宗廟門之外。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: According to ritual, the Son of Heaven weeps for those of the same surname outside the gate of the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng observes that ritual prescribes the emperor to mourn kinsmen outside the ancestral temple gate.

sentences.zh: 哭於城門，失其所也。〉

translations.literal: Weeping at the city gate misses the proper place.
translations.idiomatic: To weep at the city gate was to choose the wrong place."

sentences.zh: 五月戊寅，天子命王追尊皇祖太尉曰太王，夫人丁氏曰太王后，封王子叡爲武德侯。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on Wuyin, the Son of Heaven ordered the King posthumously to honor the Imperial Grandfather Grand Commandant as Grand King, Lady Ding as Grand Queen Mother, and to enfeoff the King's son Rui as Marquis of Wude.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on the wuyin day, the emperor authorized the King to posthumously elevate his grandfather the former Grand Commandant as "Grand King," Lady Ding as Grand Queen Mother, and to enfeoff Prince Rui as Marquis of Wude.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：以侍中鄭稱爲武德侯傅，令曰：「龍淵、太阿出昆吾之金，和氏之璧由井里之田；

translations.literal: The Wei Summary says: Appointing Palace Attendant Zheng Cheng tutor to the Marquis of Wude, an edict said: "Longyuan and Tai'e come from the metal of Kunwu; the jade disk of He Shi came from the field of Jingli;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary states that Palace Attendant Zheng Cheng was named tutor to the Marquis of Wude, with an edict declaring, "The swords Longyuan and Tai'e were forged from Kunwu ore; He's bi disk came from a common field;

sentences.zh: 礱之以砥礪，錯之以他山，故能致連城之價，爲命世之寶。

translations.literal: They are ground with whetstone and sharpened with other mountains; therefore they can achieve the price of linked cities and become treasures that command the age.
translations.idiomatic: whetted on grindstones and finished with stone from another hill—only thus could they command a city's ransom and become treasures for the age."

sentences.zh: 學亦人之砥礪也。

translations.literal: Learning is also the whetstone of men.
translations.idiomatic: Scholarship serves the same purpose for a man.

sentences.zh: 稱篤學大儒，勉以經學輔侯，宜旦夕入侍，曜明其志。」〉

translations.literal: Cheng is a sincere student and great scholar; urge him with classical learning to assist the marquis; he should attend morning and evening and brighten his aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Cheng is a devoted scholar—charge him to instruct the marquis in the classics, attending court morning and night until his purpose shines clear."

sentences.zh: 是月，馮翊山賊鄭甘、王照率衆降，皆封列侯。

translations.literal: In this month, the mountain bandits of Fengyi Zheng Gan and Wang Zhao led their masses to surrender; both were enfeoffed as full marquises.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Fengyi bandit leaders Zheng Gan and Wang Zhao surrendered with their followers, and both received marquisates.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：初，鄭甘、王照及盧水胡率其屬來降，王得降書以示朝曰：「前欲有令吾討鮮卑者，吾不從而降；

translations.literal: The Wei Book says: At first Zheng Gan, Wang Zhao, and the Lu River Hu led their dependents to surrender; the King received the surrender letter and displayed it to court saying: "Formerly there were those who wished to order Me to campaign against the Xianbei; I did not follow but they surrendered;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book recounts that when Zheng Gan, Wang Zhao, and the Lu River tribes submitted, the King read their capitulation aloud at court: "Some urged me to strike the Xianbei; I refused—and still they yielded;

sentences.zh: 又有欲使吾及今秋討盧水胡者，吾不聽，今又降。

translations.literal: there were also those who wished Me this autumn to campaign against the Lu River Hu; I did not listen, and now again they have surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: others wanted me to attack the Lu River tribes this autumn—I declined—and now they too have come in."

sentences.zh: 昔魏武侯一謀而當，有自得之色，見譏李悝。

translations.literal: Formerly Marquis Wu of Wei had one plan that hit the mark and showed a self-satisfied expression; he was ridiculed by Li Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Wu of Wei once crowed over a single clever stratagem until Li Kui mocked him for self-congratulation."

sentences.zh: 吾今說此，非自是也，徒以爲坐而降之，其功大於動兵革也。」〉

translations.literal: Now I speak this not for self-righteousness; I merely consider that sitting while they surrender—its merit is greater than moving weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: I mention this not to boast—only to note that winning submission without drawing swords surpasses any campaign."

sentences.zh: 酒泉黃華、張掖張進等各執太守以叛。

translations.literal: Huang Hua of Jiuquan, Zhang Jin of Zhangye, and others each seized their grand administrators and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hua in Jiuquan and Zhang Jin in Zhangye each detained his prefect and rose in revolt.

sentences.zh: 金城太守蘇則討進，斬之。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Jincheng Su Ze campaigned against Jin and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Ze, prefect of Jincheng, attacked Zhang Jin and executed him.

sentences.zh: 華降。

translations.literal: Hua surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hua submitted.

sentences.zh: 〈華後爲兖州刺史，見《王淩傳》。〉

translations.literal: Hua later became Inspector of Yan Province; see the biography of Wang Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hua later served as inspector of Yan Province; see the biography of Wang Ling."

sentences.zh: 六月辛亥，治兵于東郊，

translations.literal: Sixth month, Xinhai, he drilled troops at the eastern suburb,
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day in the sixth month he reviewed the troops outside the eastern suburb,

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：公卿相儀，王御華蓋，視金鼓之節。〉

translations.literal: The Wei Book says: The dukes and ministers formed his escort; the King rode under the flowered canopy and observed the cadence of bells and drums.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book describes the King touring under the ornate canopy while ministers lined his route and he watched the drum and bell signals."

sentences.zh: 庚午，遂南征。

translations.literal: On Gengwu, thereupon he campaigned south.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day he set out on the southern expedition.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：王將出征，度支中郎將新平霍性上踈諫曰：「臣聞文王與紂之事，是時天下括囊無咎，凡百君子，莫肯用訊。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary says: When the King was about to go on campaign, Libationer-General for Expenditure of Xinping Huo Xing submitted a memorial remonstrating: "Your servant has heard of the affair of King Wen and Zhou—in that age the realm tied its purse and had no blame; every gentleman refused to answer inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary records that as the King prepared to march, Huo Xing of Xinping—Director of Expenditure—submitted a memorial: "I recall King Wen and King Zhou of Shang: in those days sensible men sealed their lips and would offer no counsel.

sentences.zh: 今大王體則乾坤，廣開四聦，使賢愚各建所規。

translations.literal: Now the Great King embodies Qian and Kun, broadly opens the four openings of hearing, and causes worthy and foolish each to establish their plans.
translations.idiomatic: Today Your Highness embraces heaven and earth in person and listens on every side, inviting wise and humble alike to speak.

sentences.zh: 伏惟先王功無與比，而今能言之類，不稱爲德。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that the Former King's merit has no comparison, yet those who today can speak do not praise his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Your late father's deeds were unmatched, yet those who could praise him now withhold their voices.

sentences.zh: 故聖人曰『得百姓之歡心』。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage said: "Win the joyous hearts of the hundred families."
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying of the sages: win the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 兵書曰『戰，危事也』是以六國力戰，彊秦承弊，豳王不爭，周道用興。

translations.literal: The military books say: "War is a perilous affair"; therefore the six states fought with all their strength, strong Qin inherited their exhaustion; the lord of Bin did not contend, and the Zhou Way thereby arose.
translations.idiomatic: The military treatises call warfare perilous: the six states exhausted one another until mighty Qin inherited their weakness, whereas the house that rose from Bin avoided reckless strife and the Zhou mandate flourished.

sentences.zh: 愚謂大王且當委重本朝而守其雌，抗威虎卧，功業可成。

translations.literal: Your foolish servant considers that the Great King ought for the moment to delegate weight to this court and guard the female (yielding) side, oppose majesty and lie like a tiger—then merit and enterprise can be accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: I urge you to leave authority with the Han court for now, keep to the yielding stance of the Daoists, store your strength like a crouching tiger—then achievement will follow.

sentences.zh: 而今刱基，便復起兵，兵者凶器，必有凶擾，擾則思亂，亂出不意。

translations.literal: But now at the founding of the foundation, then again raising troops—troops are ominous instruments; there must be ominous disturbance; disturbance then thinks of chaos; chaos arises beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet you have scarcely laid your foundations and already reach for arms—yet arms breed calamity, calamity breeds unrest, unrest slides into rebellion when least expected.

sentences.zh: 臣謂此危，危於累卵。

translations.literal: Your servant considers this peril more perilous than a pile of eggs.
translations.idiomatic: To my mind this danger towers higher than a stack of eggs.

sentences.zh: 昔夏啟隱神三年，易有『不遠而復』，論有『不憚改』。

translations.literal: Formerly Xia Qi concealed the spirits three years; the Changes has "not far and return"; the Analects has "not shrink from reforming."
translations.idiomatic: When Qi of Xia mourned in seclusion for three years, the Zhou Yi promised a swift return from error, and the Analects praised those unafraid to mend their ways.

sentences.zh: 誠願大王揆古察今，深謀遠慮，與三事大夫筭其長短。

translations.literal: I sincerely wish the Great King to measure antiquity and inspect the present, plan deeply and consider far, and with the grandees of the Three Offices calculate its long and short.
translations.idiomatic: Please weigh past and present with your chief ministers and reckon every gain and loss before you march.

sentences.zh: 臣沐浴先王之遇，又初改政，復受重任，雖知言觸龍鱗，阿諛近福，竊感所誦，危而不持。

translations.literal: Your servant has bathed in the Former King's favor; moreover at the first change of government again receiving heavy responsibility—although knowing words touch dragon scales, flattery draws near fortune—I privately feel what was warned: peril yet not supporting.
translations.idiomatic: I owe everything to your father's kindness and bear fresh duties under your new rule; though I know blunt words court the dragon's wrath while flattery buys safety, I cannot stand idle while peril mounts.

sentences.zh: 」奏通，帝怒，遣刺姦就考，竟殺之。

translations.literal: " When the memorial reached him, the Emperor was angry; he dispatched the Pierce Villainy agent to conduct examination and in the end killed him.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Pi flew into a rage, handed Huo Xing to the secret police for interrogation, and had him executed.

sentences.zh: 旣而悔之，追原不及。〉

translations.literal: Afterward he regretted it, but pursuit of pardon did not reach in time.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regretted the deed, but it was too late to make amends."

sentences.zh: 秋七月庚辰，令曰：「軒轅有明臺之議，放勛有衢室之問，皆所以廣詢于下也。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Gengchen day, an edict said: "Xuanyuan had the deliberations of the Bright Tower; Fangxun had the inquiries of the Crossroads Chamber; both were means broadly to consult those below.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengchen day in the seventh month of autumn he issued an edict: "The Yellow Emperor held counsel at the Bright Tower; Yao sought opinion in the Crossroads Chamber—both widened consultation below the throne."

sentences.zh: 〈管子曰：黃帝立明臺之議者，上觀於兵也；

translations.literal: Guanzi says: The Yellow Emperor established the deliberations of the Bright Tower to observe above in military matters;
translations.idiomatic: Guanzi explains that the Yellow Emperor founded the Bright Tower deliberations to survey military affairs from on high;"

sentences.zh: 堯有衢室之問者，下聽於民也；

translations.literal: Yao had the inquiries of the Crossroads Chamber to listen below to the people;
translations.idiomatic: Yao's Crossroads Chamber let him listen downward to the common people;"

sentences.zh: 舜有告善之旌，而主不蔽也；

translations.literal: Shun had the banner for reporting good, and the ruler was not obscured;
translations.idiomatic: Shun raised a banner for good counsel so that no worthy voice stayed hidden;"

sentences.zh: 禹立建鼓於朝，而備訴訟也；

translations.literal: Yu set up the established drum at court to prepare for lawsuits;
translations.idiomatic: Yu hung the petition drum at court so grievances could be heard;"

sentences.zh: 湯有總街之廷，以觀民非也；

translations.literal: Tang had the court of the Assembly Street to observe the people's wrongs;
translations.idiomatic: Tang maintained the assembly at Total Street to expose popular complaints;"

sentences.zh: 武王有靈臺之囿，而賢者進也：此古聖帝明王所以有而勿失，得而勿忘也。〉

translations.literal: King Wu had the garden of the Spirit Terrace and worthies advanced: this is why the ancient sage emperors and enlightened kings had them and did not lose them, obtained them and did not forget them.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu's Spirit Terrace park drew worthy men forward—the ancient sage-kings instituted such institutions and never abandoned them once gained."

sentences.zh: 百官有司，其務以職盡規諫，將率陳軍法，朝士明制度，牧守申政事，縉紳考六藝，吾將兼覽焉。」

translations.literal: All officials and responsible offices, strive according to your duties to offer full remonstrance; generals set forth military law; court gentlemen clarify institutions; shepherds and guardians declare administrative affairs; gentry examine the Six Arts—I will survey them all together."
translations.idiomatic: Let every minister discharge remonstrance within his charge; let commanders publish martial regulations; court officers clarify statutes; regional governors report on administration; local elites expound the Six Classics—I shall review them all."

sentences.zh: 孫權遣使奉獻。

translations.literal: Sun Quan dispatched envoys bearing tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan sent envoys with tribute offerings.

sentences.zh: 蜀將孟達率衆降。

translations.literal: Shu general Meng Da led his masses to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu commander Meng Da surrendered with his troops.

sentences.zh: 武都氐王楊僕率種人內附，居漢陽郡。

translations.literal: Di king Yang Pu of Wudu led his tribesmen to attach inward and dwell in Hanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Pu, king of the Di in Wudu, led his people to submit and was settled in Hanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》載王自手筆令曰：「吾前遣使宣國威靈，而達即來。

translations.literal: The Wei Summary carries the King's personally brush-written edict saying: "Formerly I dispatched envoys to proclaim the state's awesome power and spiritual efficacy, and Da thereupon came.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary preserves the King's own brush order: "When I sent envoys abroad to display Wei majesty, Meng Da came at once to surrender."

sentences.zh: 吾惟春秋襃儀父，即封拜達，使還領新城太守。

translations.literal: I consider how the Spring and Autumn Annals praised Yifu of Zhu—thereupon I enfeoff and appoint Da, ordering him to return and hold the post of Grand Administrator of Xincheng.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the Spring and Autumn Annals honored Yifu of Zhu, I now enfeoff Meng Da and send him back to serve as prefect of Xincheng.

sentences.zh: 近復有扶老攜幼首向王化者。

translations.literal: Recently again there are those supporting the aged and leading the young who turn their heads toward royal transformation.
translations.idiomatic: More families—old and young together—have lately come forward to accept imperial rule.

sentences.zh: 吾聞夙沙之民自縛其君以歸神農，豳國之衆襁負其子而入酆、鎬，斯豈驅略迫脅之所致哉？

translations.literal: I have heard that the people of Sushen bound their own ruler to submit to Shennong, and that the multitudes of Bin carried their children on their backs and entered Feng and Hao—is this caused by driving, plundering, or coercion?
translations.idiomatic: I read that the Sushen people bound their lord and delivered him to Shennong, and that the folk of Bin swaddled their infants and thronged into Feng and Hao—such movements were never forced marches at spearpoint.

sentences.zh: 乃風化動其情而仁義感其衷，歡心內發使之然也。

translations.literal: It is transformation by moral influence moving their feelings and benevolence and righteousness stirring their inner hearts; joyous hearts issuing from within make it so.
translations.idiomatic: Moral sway stirred their hearts and humanity moved them inwardly until glad consent rose of itself—that is why they came.

sentences.zh: 以此而推，西南將萬里無外，權、備將與誰守死乎？」〉

translations.literal: Extrapolating from this, the southwest will be without outsiders for ten thousand li—Quan and Bei—with whom will they defend to the death?"
translations.idiomatic: If this holds, the southwest will fold into the realm from border to border—which ally could Sun Quan or Liu Bei still rally for a doomed defense?"

sentences.zh: 甲午，軍次于譙，大饗六軍及譙父老百姓于邑東。

translations.literal: On Jiawu, the army halted at Qiao and feasted the six armies and the elders and common people of Qiao east of the walled town.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day the host camped at Qiao and gave a grand banquet for the six armies and for the elders and townsfolk east of the city.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：設伎樂百戲，令曰：「先王皆樂其所生，禮不忘其本。

translations.literal: The Wei Book says: They set up performers and hundred entertainments; an edict said: "Former kings all delighted in their birthplace; ritual does not forget its roots.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book records musicians and variety acts; an edict declared, "Ancient kings celebrated their native soil; ceremony never forgets its origins."

sentences.zh: 譙，霸王之邦，真人本出，其復譙租稅二年。

translations.literal: Qiao is the land of hegemons; the True Man originally emerged from it—there shall be remission of Qiao's land tax for two years.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao bred founders of empire—the sage king himself sprang from here—so its taxes are remitted for two years."

sentences.zh: 」三老吏民上壽，日夕而罷。

translations.literal: " The sanlao, clerks, and people presented longevity congratulations; at day's end they ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The elder worthies, officials, and commoners toasted his longevity, and the revelry lasted until evening."

sentences.zh: 丙申，親祠譙陵。

translations.literal: On Bingshen, he personally sacrificed at the mausoleum at Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day he personally offered sacrifice at the imperial tombs near Qiao.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：昔者先王之以孝治天下也，內節天性，外施四海，存盡其敬，亡極其哀，思慕諒闇，寄政冢宰，故曰「三年之喪，自天子達于庶人」。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: Formerly the former kings used filial piety to govern the realm—internally regulating heavenly nature, externally extending through the four seas; while alive they exhausted reverence, in death they exhausted grief; longing and mourning in silent darkness in the chamber, entrusting government to the grand steward—therefore it is said "the three-year mourning, from the Son of Heaven reaches to the common people."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng observes that the ancient kings ruled through filial duty: they cultivated innate virtue within and extended humanity across the realm; they honored the living to the utmost and mourned the dead without stint; during the silent vigil they yielded governance to the chief minister—hence the maxim that three years' mourning binds emperor and commoner alike.

sentences.zh: 夫然，故在三之義惇，臣子之恩篤，雍熙之化隆，經國之道固，聖人之所以通天地，厚人倫，顯至教，敦風俗，斯萬世不易之典，百王服膺之制也。

translations.literal: Being so, therefore the meaning of "being thrice honored" is earnest, the kindness of ministers and sons is deep, the transformation of harmonious brilliance is lofty, the way of ordering the state is firm—this is why sages communicate with Heaven and Earth, enrich human relationships, display utmost teaching, and encourage customs—this is the norm unchanging for myriad ages, the system embraced by the hundred kings.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the three-year rite carried real weight, subjects and sons repaid it in full, harmony spread and the state stood firm—by this the sages joined Heaven and earth, deepened the human bonds, proclaimed the highest teaching, and shaped the customs: an unchanging model that every throne has honored.

sentences.zh: 是故喪禮素冠，鄶人著庶見之譏，宰予降朞，仲尼發不仁之歎，子頹忘戚，君子以爲樂禍，魯侯易服，春秋知其不終，豈不以墜至痛之誠心，喪哀樂之大節者哉？

translations.literal: Therefore in mourning ritual the plain cap—the people of Kuai earned ridicule for seeing the multitude; Zai Yu shortened the single-year period—Zhongni issued sighs of lacking benevolence; Zitui forgot sorrow—the gentleman considered it rejoicing in calamity; the Marquis of Lu changed garments—the Spring and Autumn Annals knew he would not end well—is it not because they fell from utmost painful sincerity and lost the great norms of grief and joy?
translations.idiomatic: Hence undyed caps in mourning earned Kuai mockery for premature court appearances; Zai Yu's shortened mourning drew Confucius's charge of heartlessness; Prince Tui's levity showed delight in disaster; the Duke of Lu's change of dress foretold ruin in the Annals—all betrayed genuine grief and violated the great rhythms of sorrow and joy.

sentences.zh: 故雖三季之末，七雄之弊，猶未有廢縗斬於旬朔之閒，釋麻杖於反哭之日者也。

translations.literal: Therefore though at the end of the three final ages, in the defects of the seven powers, still there was none who discarded hemp mourning within ten-day or month intervals, or released hemp staff on the day of returning to weep.
translations.idiomatic: Even in the decadent ages of the three final dynasties and the strife of the seven powers, no one cast off sackcloth within weeks or laid aside the mourning staff on the day of the "returning lament."

sentences.zh: 逮于漢文，變易古制，人道之紀，一旦而廢，縗素奪於至尊，四海散其遏密，義感闕於羣后，大化墜於君親；

translations.literal: Down to Emperor Wen of Han, altering the ancient system, the norms of human relations in one morning were abolished; sackcloth was wrested by the supreme honor; the four seas scattered their solemn silence; righteous emotion failed among the host of lords; great transformation fell from ruler and parent;
translations.idiomatic: Then Emperor Wen of Han rewrote the old code: human duties collapsed overnight—mourning dress could be stripped by imperial fiat, the realm lost its solemn silence, regional lords ceased to feel moral awe, and the great moral order slipped between sovereign and kin;

sentences.zh: 雖心存貶約，慮在經綸，至於樹德垂聲，崇化變俗，固以道薄於當年，風穨於百代矣。

translations.literal: although in heart there was intent to reduce and restrain, concern lay in ordering the realm—as for establishing virtue and leaving reputation, exalting transformation and altering customs, fundamentally the Way was thin in that age, and wind declined for hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: however thrifty his motives or urgent his statecraft, his fame for virtue and power to reform customs ran thin—the Way waned in his day and left posterity adrift.

sentences.zh: 且武王載主而牧野不陣，晉襄墨縗而三帥爲俘，應務濟功，服其焉害。

translations.literal: Moreover King Wu carried the spirit tablet yet did not array troops at Muye; Jin Xiang wore ink mourning yet the three commanders became captives—responding to affairs and aiding merit, what harm do they submit to?
translations.idiomatic: King Wu carried his father's spirit tablet into battle yet avoided a pitched clash at Muye; Duke Xiang of Jin wore ink-stained sackcloth yet yielded three generals as prisoners—great emergencies sometimes bend ritual; what harm came of it?

sentences.zh: 魏王旣追漢制，替其大禮，處莫重之哀而設饗宴之樂，居貽厥之始而墜王化之基，及至受禪，顯納二女，忘其至恤以誣先聖之典，天心喪矣，將何以終！

translations.literal: The King of Wei having followed Han regulations, replaced its great rites—being in the grief of nothing heavier yet setting up feast music; dwelling at the beginning of handing down yet dropping the foundation of royal transformation; reaching to receiving abdication, openly taking in two daughters—forgetting utmost sorrow and falsifying the canons of former sages—Heaven's heart is lost—how will he end!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the King of Wei adopted Han's lax precedent: amid the gravest bereavement he staged feasts and music; at the very founding of his line he undercut royal virtue; at the abdication he brazenly took two imperial daughters—forgetting deepest grief and mocking the sages' teaching. Heaven's favor was forfeited—how could such a reign close well?

sentences.zh: 是以知王齡之不遐，卜世之期促也。〉

translations.literal: From this one knows the King's years were not far-reaching; the divined generations' period was short.
translations.idiomatic: Small wonder his reign proved short and his dynasty's allotted span ran thin."

sentences.zh: 八月，石邑縣言鳳皇集。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Shiyi County reported phoenixes assembled.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Shiyi County reported phoenixes gathering.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月癸卯，令曰：「諸將征伐，士卒死亡者或未收斂，吾甚哀之；

translations.literal: Winter, eleventh month, on Guimao, an edict said: "When the various generals campaign and soldiers die, sometimes they are not gathered for burial—I deeply grieve for them;
translations.idiomatic: On the guimao day in the eleventh month of winter he issued an edict: "When armies march, fallen soldiers are sometimes left unburied—I mourn them bitterly;"

sentences.zh: 其告郡國給槥

translations.literal: let it be announced to the commanderies and kingdoms to supply hui (coffins)
translations.idiomatic: instruct every commandery and principality to issue coffins

sentences.zh: 〈槥音衞〉

translations.literal: 〈 hui is pronounced wei 〉
translations.idiomatic: Pronunciation gloss: the character (hui) is read the same as the common word wei, "defend."

sentences.zh: 櫝殯斂，送致其家，官爲設祭。」

translations.literal: enclosed burial receptacles for laying out and dressing the dead, convey them to their homes, and let officials perform sacrifices for them."
translations.idiomatic: For encoffining and laying out the remains, ship each body home, and let the officials sponsor the sacrificial offerings."

sentences.zh: 〈《漢書》高祖八月令曰：「士卒從軍死，爲槥。

translations.literal: The Han Book August edict of Emperor Gaozu said: "Soldiers who die following the army—supply hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Han shu quotes Emperor Gaozu's eighth-month decree: "Men who die on campaign shall receive a burial coffin (hui).

sentences.zh: 」應劭曰：「槥，小棺也，今謂之櫝。

translations.literal: " Ying Shao said: "Hui is a small coffin; nowadays it is called du (case).
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao glosses: "Hui is a small coffin—today we call it a case (du)."

sentences.zh: 」應璩百一詩曰：「槥車在道路，征夫不得休。

translations.literal: " Ying Qu's Hundred and One Poem says: "The hui cart is on the road; the campaigner cannot rest.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Qu's "Hundred and One" poems say: "Coffin wagons line the roads while conscripts never rest."

sentences.zh: 」陸機大墓賦曰：「觀細木而悶遲，覩洪櫝而念槥。」〉

translations.literal: " Lu Ji's Rhapsody on the Great Tomb says: "Gazing on fine wood I am depressed and slow; beholding a great case I think of hui."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's Rhapsody on a Princely Tomb says: "The sight of plain boards brought gloom; the great outer coffin recalled the simple hui.""

sentences.zh: 丙午，行至曲蠡。

translations.literal: On Bingwu, traveling reached Quli.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingwu day he marched as far as Quli.

sentences.zh: 是歲，長水校尉戴陵諫不宜數行弋獵，帝大怒；

translations.literal: In this year, Commandant of Changshui Dai Ling remonstrated that one should not frequently go on hawking and hunting; the Emperor was greatly angry;
translations.idiomatic: That year Commandant of the Changshui encampment Dai Ling urged the emperor to stop his repeated hunting sorties, and the emperor flew into a rage;

sentences.zh: 陵減死罪一等。

translations.literal: Ling's capital crime was reduced by one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Ling's sentence was commuted one rank below death.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，郊祀天地、明堂。

translations.literal: Second year, spring, first month, suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth and the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the second year (Huangchu 2, 221 CE) he performed the suburban sacrifice to Heaven and Earth at the Bright Hall.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，校獵至原陵，遣使者以太牢祠漢世祖。

translations.literal: On Jiaxu, hunt-inspection reached Yuanling; he dispatched envoys to sacrifice the grand beast to Han Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day the imperial hunt reached Yuanling, where he sent envoys to offer the grand sacrifice at Emperor Guangwu's tomb.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，朝日于東郊。

translations.literal: On Yihai, court audience with the sun at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day he greeted the sun at the eastern suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之以爲禮天子以春分朝日，秋分夕月；

translations.literal: Your subject Song Zhi considers that by ritual the Son of Heaven audience with the sun at the spring equinox, evening moon at the autumn equinox;
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi notes that ritual prescribes the emperor's salutation of the sun at the spring equinox and of the moon at the autumn equinox;

sentences.zh: 尋此年正月郊祀，有月無日，乙亥朝日，則有日無月，蓋文之脫也。

translations.literal: Examining this year's first month suburban sacrifice, there is month without day; Yihai audience with sun, then there is day without month—probably text omission.
translations.idiomatic: here the suburban rite for the first month records the month but no cyclical day, while the solar ceremony records yihai without naming the month—likely a scribal omission.

sentences.zh: 案明帝朝日夕月，皆如禮文，故知此紀爲誤者也。〉

translations.literal: Examining Ming Di's audience with sun and evening moon, both accord with ritual text; therefore know this annals entry is erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: Mingdi's later observances followed the canonical calendar exactly, which confirms this entry is mistaken."

sentences.zh: 初令郡國口滿十萬者，歲察孝廉一人；

translations.literal: First ordinance: commanderies and kingdoms whose population reaches one hundred thousand shall yearly investigate one filially pious and incorrupt;
translations.idiomatic: He first decreed that any commandery or kingdom with a population of one hundred thousand could nominate one Filially Pious and Incorrupt candidate each year;

sentences.zh: 其有秀異，無拘戶口。

translations.literal: if there are outstanding exceptional persons, do not restrict by household registers.
translations.idiomatic: truly outstanding talent might be recommended regardless of household quota.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，分三公戶邑，封子弟各一人爲列侯。

translations.literal: On Xinsi, he divided the households and towns of the Three Dukes and enfeoffed one son or younger relative each as full marquis.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinsi day he carved lands from the Three Excellencies' patrimonies to enfeoff one son or nephew of each as full marquis.

sentences.zh: 壬午，復潁川郡一年田租。

translations.literal: On Renwu, remitted Yingchuan commandery one year's field rent.
translations.idiomatic: On the renwu day he remitted one year's land tax for Yingchuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載詔曰：「潁川，先帝所由起兵征伐也。

translations.literal: The Wei Book carries an edict saying: "Yingchuan is where the Former Emperor raised troops and campaigned.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book preserves an edict: "Yingchuan was the furnace from which the late emperor launched his wars.

sentences.zh: 官渡之役，四方瓦解，遠近顧望，而此郡守義，丁壯荷戈，老弱負糧。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Guandu, the four directions collapsed like tiles; far and near looked about—but this commandery kept righteousness; stalwart men bore halberds, old and weak bore grain.
translations.idiomatic: When Guandu shattered every ally and neighbors hedged their bets, Yingchuan alone stood firm—every able man shouldered arms while elders hauled grain.

sentences.zh: 昔漢祖以秦中爲國本，光武恃河內爲王基，今朕復於此登壇受禪，天以此郡翼成大魏。」〉

translations.literal: Formerly Han Gaozu took Qinzhong as national foundation; Guangwu relied on Henei as royal foundation; now I again at this place ascend the altar and receive abdication—Heaven by this commandery wings the completion of great Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Han Gaozu built his realm on the Guanzhong basin; Guangwu trusted Henei as his base—here I ascended the altar to receive the abdication. Heaven uses this commandery to uphold Great Wei."

sentences.zh: 改許縣爲許昌縣。

translations.literal: Changed Xu county to Xuchang county.
translations.idiomatic: Xu county was renamed Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 以魏郡東部爲陽平郡，西部爲廣平郡。

translations.literal: Taking Wei's eastern division as Yangping commandery, western division as Guangping commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern precinct of Wei commandery became Yangping commandery and the western precinct Guangping commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》曰：改長安、譙、許昌、鄴、洛陽爲五都；

translations.literal: The Wei Summary says: Chang'an, Qiao, Xuchang, Ye, and Luoyang were changed to be the Five Capitals;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary adds that Chang'an, Qiao, Xuchang, Ye, and Luoyang were designated the "five capitals";"

sentences.zh: 立石表，西界宜陽，北循太行，東北界陽平，南循魯陽，東界郯，爲中都之地。

translations.literal: Stone markers were erected: west bounded Yiyang, north followed Taihang, northeast bounded Yangping, south followed Luyang, east bounded Tan—these formed the central capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Stone pillars marked the inner capital belt—west to Yiyang, north along the Taihang range, northeast to Yangping, south through Luyang, east to Tan.

sentences.zh: 令天下聽內徙，復五年，後又增其復。〉

translations.literal: Ordered the realm permitted to migrate inward, exempt five years, afterward again increased the exemption.
translations.idiomatic: People were encouraged to settle inside the belt with five-year tax relief, later extended further."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「昔仲尼資大聖之才，懷帝王之器，當衰周之末，無受命之運，在魯、衞之朝，教化乎洙、泗之上，悽悽焉，遑遑焉，欲屈己以存道，貶身以救世。

translations.literal: An edict said: "Formerly Zhongni possessed the talents of a grand sage, embraced the instruments of emperor and king; facing the end of declining Zhou, lacking the fate of receiving the mandate; in the courts of Lu and Wei, transforming and teaching above Zhu and Si—mournfully, urgently—wishing to bend himself to preserve the Way, depreciate himself to save the age.
translations.idiomatic: An edict proclaimed: "Confucius bore the gifts of a supreme sage and the bearing of a king, yet at Zhou's twilight lacked Heaven's mandate; he wandered Lu and Wei and taught beside the Zhu and Si streams—restless, sorrowful—ready to humble himself to preserve the Way and risk reputation to redeem the world.

sentences.zh: 于時王公終莫能用之，乃退考五代之禮，脩素王之事，因魯史而制春秋，就太師而正雅頌，俾千載之後，莫不宗其文以述作，仰其聖以成謀，咨！

translations.literal: At that time kings and dukes finally none could employ him; thereupon he retired to investigate the rites of five dynasties, cultivate the affairs of the Uncrowned King, relying on Lu's chronicles to compose Spring and Autumn, approaching the Grand Music Master to rectify Ya and Song—causing after a thousand ages none not to honor his texts for narration and composition, look up to his sagehood to complete plans—alas!
translations.idiomatic: When no throne would employ him, he withdrew to study the rituals of five ages and assumed the mantle of the uncrowned king—distilling the Spring and Autumn Annals from Lu's archives and tuning the Hymns with the grand music master—so that later ages treat his words as scripture for authorship and look to his sagacity as the measure of policy—oh!

sentences.zh: 可謂命世之大聖，億載之師表者也。

translations.literal: Can be called the grand sage who commanded the age, the teacher and model for hundred million generations.
translations.idiomatic: Truly he was the sage who defined his epoch and the teacher for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 遭天下大亂，百祀墮壞，舊居之廟，毀而不脩，襃成之後，絕而莫繼，闕里不聞講頌之聲，四時不覩蒸甞之位，斯豈所謂崇禮報功，盛德百世必祀者哉！

translations.literal: Meeting great chaos in the realm, hundred sacrifices fell and ruined; the temple of his old dwelling destroyed and not repaired; after Baocheng cut off with none to continue; Que lane does not hear sounds of lecture and praise; four seasons do not observe steaming-tasting positions—is this what is called exalting ritual and repaying merit, splendid virtue must be sacrificed for hundred generations!
translations.idiomatic: Empire-wide turmoil shattered his cult: the hometown shrine lies in ruins unbuilt; Baocheng's line died out with no heir; no lectures echo in Queli and seasonal offerings miss the steaming rites—can this honor the teaching that ranks merit above all and demands perpetual sacrifice for supreme virtue?

sentences.zh: 其以議郎孔羨爲宗聖侯，邑百戶，奉孔子祀。

translations.literal: Let Gentleman Consultant Kong Xian be made Marquis Zongsheng, fief one hundred households, to attend Confucius's sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Gentleman Consultant Kong Xian is therefore named Marquis who Honors the Sage with a hundred-household fief to maintain Confucian sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 」令魯郡脩起舊廟，置百戶吏卒以守衞之，又於其外廣爲室屋以居學者。

translations.literal: " Order Lu commandery to restore and raise the old temple, establish one hundred households of clerks and soldiers to guard it; moreover beyond it broadly build chambers and houses to house scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Lu commandery shall rebuild the ancient temple, station a guard of a hundred households, and erect dormitories round about for students."

sentences.zh: 三月，加遼東太守公孫恭爲車騎將軍。

translations.literal: Third month, advanced Liaodong Grand Administrator Gongsun Gong to General of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Liaodong prefect Gongsun Gong was promoted to General of Chariots and Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 初復五銖錢。

translations.literal: First restoration of the five-zhu coin.
translations.idiomatic: The five-zhu copper coin was restored to circulation.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，以車騎將軍曹仁爲大將軍。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, taking General of Chariots and Cavalry Cao Ren as Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer General of Chariots and Cavalry Cao Ren was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 五月，鄭甘復叛，遣曹仁討斬之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, Zheng Gan again rebelled; dispatched Cao Ren to campaign and behead him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Zheng Gan rebelled again; Cao Ren was sent to crush him and took his head.

sentences.zh: 六月庚子，初祀五嶽四瀆，咸秩羣祀。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Gengzi day, first sacrifice to the Five Marchmounts and Four Streams—all ranks of sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day in the sixth month he sacrificed for the first time to the Five Sacred Peaks and Four Great Rivers and ordered all lesser cults regulated.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》：甲辰，以京師宗廟未成，帝親祠武皇帝于建始殿，躬執饋奠，如家人之禮。〉

translations.literal: Wei Book: On Jiachen, because the capital ancestral temple was not completed, the Emperor personally sacrificed to Martial Emperor at Jianshi Hall, personally holding offering presentation like family ritual.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book notes that on the jiachen day—ancestral shrines in the capital still unfinished—the emperor sacrificed to Emperor Wu in Jianshi Hall, personally presenting offerings as though among kin."

sentences.zh: 丁卯，夫人甄氏卒。

translations.literal: On Dingmao, Lady Zhen died.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingmao day Lady Zhen died.

sentences.zh: 戊辰晦，日有食之，有司奏免太尉，詔曰：「災異之作，以譴元首，而歸過股肱，豈禹、湯罪己之義乎？

translations.literal: Last day of month Wuchen, there was solar eclipse; responsible offices memorialized to dismiss Grand Commandant; edict said: "When prodigies arise, to blame the chief and shift fault to limbs—is this the meaning of Yu and Tang blaming themselves?
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the month (wuchen) an eclipse occurred; officials urged the Grand Commandant's dismissal, but an edict replied: "Omens reprimand the sovereign—how does blaming my ministers match the spirit of Yu and Tang reproaching themselves?

sentences.zh: 其令百官各虔厥職，後有天地之眚，勿復劾三公。」

translations.literal: Let it order the hundred officials each reverently their duties; afterward if there are calamities of Heaven and Earth, do not again impeach the Three Dukes."
translations.idiomatic: Let every minister fulfill his duty with care; when Heaven sends warning again, do not impeach the Three Excellencies."

sentences.zh: 三年春正月丙寅朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: Third year spring first month Bingyin new moon day, there was solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the first month of the third year (bingyin) there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 庚午，行幸許昌宮。

translations.literal: On Gengwu, progressed to favor Xuchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengwu day he traveled to Xuchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「今之計考，古之貢士也；

translations.literal: Edict said: "Today's examination reckoning is ancient tribute scholars;
translations.idiomatic: An edict declared: "Today's merit examinations are the descendant of the Han tribute-student system;

sentences.zh: 十室之邑，必有忠信，若限年然後取士，是呂尚、周晉不顯於前世也。

translations.literal: In a village of ten houses there must be loyalty and trustworthiness—if limiting by age then selecting scholars, this is Lü Shang and Zhou Jin not appearing in former generations.
translations.idiomatic: even a hamlet of ten holds loyal talent—if we insist on age quotas, men like Lü Shang would never have risen in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 其令郡國所選，勿拘老幼；

translations.literal: Let it order commanderies and kingdoms' selections not bound old and young;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore commanderies must nominate candidates without regard to age;

sentences.zh: 儒通經術，吏達文法，到皆試用。

translations.literal: Ru who penetrate classics techniques, clerks who comprehend documentary law—when arrived all trial employ.
translations.idiomatic: classicists must master the canon, clerks must know statutes—every nominee serves on probation.

sentences.zh: 有司糾故不以實者。」

translations.literal: Responsible offices investigate deliberately not according to reality."
translations.idiomatic: Officials who falsify nominations will be prosecuted."

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：癸亥，孫權上書，說：「劉備支黨四萬人，馬二三千匹，出秭歸，請往埽撲，以克捷爲效。

translations.literal: Wei Book says: On Guihai, Sun Quan submitted memorial saying: "Liu Bei's branch faction forty thousand men, horses two or three thousand, have gone out from Zigui; please permit going to sweep and strike, taking victory as effect.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book notes that on the guihai day Sun Quan wrote in to report: "Liu Bei's lieutenants—some forty thousand men and two or three thousand horses—have marched out of Zigui; allow me to strike them down and I will report victory."

sentences.zh: 」帝報曰：「昔隗嚻之弊，禍發栒邑，子陽之禽，變起扞關，將軍其亢厲威武，勉蹈奇功，以稱吾意。」〉

translations.literal: " The Emperor replied saying: "Formerly Wei Xiao's defeat, calamity arose at Xunyi; Ziyang's capture, change arose at Han Pass—General, raise fierce martial power, strive to tread strange merit, to match My intention."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered: "Wei Xiao fell when disaster struck Xunyi; Gongsun Shu was caught when lines collapsed at Han Pass—marshal your forces with vigor, seize the chance for a decisive blow, and satisfy my hopes."

sentences.zh: 二月，鄯善、龜茲、于闐王各遣使奉獻，詔曰：「西戎即叙，氐、羌來王，詩、書美之。

translations.literal: Second month, kings of Shanshan, Qiuci, and Yutian each dispatched envoys bearing tribute; edict said: "Western Rong brought to order, Di and Qiang came to be kings—the Poetry and Documents praise this.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the kings of Shanshan, Kucha, and Khotan each sent tribute; an edict ran: "The Documents praise how the western tribes were pacified and the Di and Qiang came to court.

sentences.zh: 頃者西域外夷並款塞內附，

translations.literal: Recently Western Regions outer barbarians together sincerely blocked gates inward attachment,
translations.idiomatic: Now the outer peoples beyond the Western Regions have knocked at the frontier posts asking to submit;

sentences.zh: 〈應劭《

translations.literal: 〈 Ying Shao 《
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's commentary on the

sentences.zh: 〈漢書〉

translations.literal: 〈Han Book〉
translations.idiomatic: Book of Han

sentences.zh: 注》曰：款，叩也；

translations.literal: Commentary》 says: Kuan means knock;
translations.idiomatic: explains that kuan means knocking at the barrier gates;

sentences.zh: 皆叩塞門來服從。〉

translations.literal: all knock barrier gates coming to submit.
translations.idiomatic: they all beat on the barrier gates seeking allegiance."

sentences.zh: 其遣使者撫勞之。

translations.literal: Let envoys be dispatched to soothe and labor them.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch envoys to console and reward them.

sentences.zh: 」是後西域遂通，置戊己校尉。

translations.literal: " After this the Western Regions then opened; established Wuji Colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Traffic with the west was thereafter regular, and the Wuji colonel was appointed to oversee it."

sentences.zh: 三月乙丑，立齊公叡爲平原王，帝弟鄢陵公彰等十一人皆爲王。

translations.literal: Third month Yichou, established Duke of Qi Rui as Prince of Pingyuan; eleven persons including the Emperor's younger brother Duke of Yanling Zhang all became kings.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day in the third month Prince Rui of Qi was raised to Prince of Pingyuan, and eleven imperial brothers—including Zhang, Duke of Yanling—were invested as kings.

sentences.zh: 初制封王之庶子爲鄉公，嗣王之庶子爲亭侯，公之庶子爲亭伯。

translations.literal: First regulation: enfeoff kings' secondary sons as district dukes, heir kings' secondary sons as village marquises, dukes' secondary sons as village earls.
translations.idiomatic: New rules fixed that a king's younger sons receive district-duke rank, a successor king's younger sons village marquisates, and a duke's younger sons village earldoms.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，立皇子霖爲河東王。

translations.literal: On Jiaxu, established Imperial Son Lin as Prince of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiaxu day Prince Lin was named Prince of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 甲午，行幸襄邑。

translations.literal: On Jiawu, progressed to favor Xiangyi.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day he traveled to Xiangyi.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊申，立鄄城侯植爲鄄城王。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month Wushen, established Marquis of Juancheng Zhi as Prince of Juancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day in the fourth month of summer Cao Zhi was promoted from Marquis to Prince of Juancheng.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，行還許昌宮。

translations.literal: On Guihai, progressed returning to Xuchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the guihai day he returned to Xuchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 五月，以荊、揚、江表八郡爲荊州，孫權領牧故也；

translations.literal: Fifth month, taking Jing, Yang, eight commanderies south of the river as Jing Province—because Sun Quan held governorship;
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month eight commanderies south of the Yangzi were grouped into a new Jing province because Sun Quan already styled himself its governor;

sentences.zh: 荊州江北諸郡爲郢州。

translations.literal: Jing Province north of the river various commanderies became Ying Province.
translations.idiomatic: the commanderies north of the Great River became Ying province.

sentences.zh: 閏月，孫權破劉備於夷陵。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, Sun Quan defeated Liu Bei at Yiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Sun Quan defeated Liu Bei at Yiling.

sentences.zh: 初，帝聞備兵東下，與權交戰，樹柵連營七百餘里，謂羣臣曰：「備不曉兵，豈有七百里營可以拒敵者乎！

translations.literal: At first, when the Emperor heard Bei's troops went east down, battling with Quan, planting palisades linking camps over seven hundred li, he said to the host of ministers: "Bei does not understand warfare—how can there be seven hundred li of camp that can resist the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, learning that Liu Bei had marched east to fight Sun Quan and had planted linked camps along seven hundred li of riverbank, Cao Pi told his ministers, "Liu Bei knows nothing of war—who ever defended a seven-hundred-li palisade?

sentences.zh: 『苞原隰險阻而爲軍者，爲敵所禽』，此兵忌也。

translations.literal: 'Wrapping plains and marshes, perilous defiles to make army—by enemy captured'—this is military taboo.
translations.idiomatic: The Art of War warns that camping across marshes and broken ground invites capture—that is elementary doctrine.

sentences.zh: 孫權上事今至矣。

translations.literal: Sun Quan's upward report now arrives.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's dispatch should arrive any day now."

sentences.zh: 」後七日，破備書到。

translations.literal: " After seven days, the letter defeating Bei arrived.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later the bulletin of Liu Bei's defeat reached court.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，冀州大蝗，民饑，使尚書杜畿持節開倉廩以振之。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, Ji Province great locusts, people hungry; ordered Supervisor of the Secretariat Du Ji bearing insignia to open granaries to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn locusts devastated Ji province and famine spread; Du Ji, Minister of the Secretariat, opened the granaries with imperial credentials to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 八月，蜀大將黃權率衆降。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Shu great general Huang Quan led masses to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Shu general Huang Quan surrendered with his army.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：權及領南郡太守史郃等三百一十八人，詣荊州刺史奉上所假印綬、棨戟、幢麾、牙門、鼓車。

translations.literal: Wei Book says: Quan and concurrent Nan Grand Administrator Shi He and others three hundred eighteen persons, went to Jing Province Inspector presenting lent seal-cords, banner halberds, standard banners, gate-of-teeth, drum carts.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book records that Huang Quan and Acting Prefect of Nan commandery Shi He—318 men in all—presented themselves to the inspector of Jing province and returned their borrowed seals, ceremonial halberds, command banners, gate insignia, and drum carts.

sentences.zh: 權等詣行在所，帝置酒設樂，引見於承光殿。

translations.literal: Quan and others went to the traveling encampment; the Emperor set wine and established music, led audience at Chengguang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: They were summoned to the emperor's mobile court, where he hosted a banquet with music and received them in Chengguang Hall.

sentences.zh: 權、郃等人人前自陳，帝爲論說軍旅成敗去就之分，諸將無不喜恱。

translations.literal: Quan, He and others each person forward personally stated; the Emperor for them discussed military hosts success and failure, going and staying distinctions—the various generals none not joyful.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan, Shi He, and their officers stepped forward to speak; the emperor lectured them on the fortunes of war and the choices that lay before them, and every officer left satisfied.

sentences.zh: 賜權金帛、車馬、衣裘、帷帳、妻妾，下及偏裨皆有差。

translations.literal: Bestowed on Quan gold, silk, carriages, horses, robes, furs, curtains, tents, wives and concubines; down to deputy commanders all had gradations.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan received gold, silk, mounts, furs, tents, and household attendants in graded gifts that extended down to his subordinate officers.

sentences.zh: 拜權爲侍中鎮南將軍，封列侯，即日召使驂乘；

translations.literal: Appointed Quan as Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the South, enfeoffed as full marquis, same day summoned to ride as third rider;
translations.idiomatic: Huang Quan was named Palace Attendant and General Who Guards the South, invested as a full marquis, and summoned that same day to ride beside the emperor in the carriage.

sentences.zh: 及封史郃等四十二人皆爲列侯，爲將軍郎將百餘人。〉

translations.literal: And enfeoffed Shi He and others forty-two persons all as full marquis; made generals and Chief and lieutenant generals over a hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-two others including Shi He received marquisates, and more than a hundred were commissioned as generals or colonels.

sentences.zh: 九月甲午，詔曰：「夫婦人與政，亂之本也。

translations.literal: Ninth month Jiawu, edict said: "When women participate in government, it is the root of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiawu day in the ninth month an edict declared: "When women meddle in government, disorder takes root.

sentences.zh: 自今以後，羣臣不得奏事太后，后族之家不得當輔政之任，又不得橫受茅土之爵；

translations.literal: From now after, host of ministers may not memorialize affairs to Empress Dowager; empress clan households may not hold assistant regency duties, nor recklessly receive straw-earth noble ranks;
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth ministers shall not route state business through the empress dowager; no maternal relatives may serve as regents or receive large fiefs without merit;

sentences.zh: 以此詔傳後世，若有背違，天下共誅之。」
