translations.idiomatic: publish this as perpetual law—whoever breaks it may be punished by all the realm."

sentences.zh: 〈孫盛曰：夫經國營治，必憑俊喆之輔，賢達令德，必居參亂之任，故雖周室之盛，有婦人與焉。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: Ordering state and managing governance must rely on wise assistants; worthy attained excellent virtue must occupy counsel-participation duties—therefore though Zhou house flourished, there were women therein.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng argues that ruling well requires wise ministers and that worthy advisers hold deliberative posts—even at Zhou's height women took part in council.

sentences.zh: 然則坤道承天，南面罔二，三從之禮，謂之至順，至於號令自天子出，奏事專行，非古義也。

translations.literal: Yet kun way receives heaven, facing south without second; three obediences ritual called utmost compliance—as for commands issuing from Son of Heaven, memorializing affairs exclusively practiced—not ancient meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Earth's virtue yields to Heaven; the ruler faces south alone; the "three obediences" define proper submission—but edicts must stem from the emperor alone, and memorials routed solely through a dowager breaks classical precedent.

sentences.zh: 昔在申、呂，實匡有周。

translations.literal: Formerly at Shen and Lü, truly aided Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The houses of Shen and Lü once strengthened Zhou.

sentences.zh: 苟以天下爲心，惟德是杖，則親疏之授，至公一也，何至后族而必斥遠之哉？

translations.literal: If taking all-under-heaven as heart, only virtue as staff—then intimate and distant appointments utmost fairness are one—why reach empress kin and necessarily reject them far?
translations.idiomatic: If appointments serve the realm and rest on virtue alone, kin and stranger alike should be judged impartially—why ban maternal relatives outright?

sentences.zh: 二漢之季世，王道陵遲，故令外戚憑寵，職爲亂階。

translations.literal: Two Han's final generations, kingly way declined delayed—therefore caused outer kin relying on favor, duty becoming steps of disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han the royal way decayed, so in-laws leveraged favor until they became rungs on the ladder to chaos.

sentences.zh: 於此，自時昏道喪，運祚將移，縱無王、呂之難，豈乏田、趙之禍乎？

translations.literal: At this, from time dark way lost, fate tablet about to shift—even without Wang and Lü disasters, how lack Tian and Zhao calamities?
translations.idiomatic: Once government grew dark and the mandate shifted, even without a Wang Mang or Lü Hou there were still disasters like Tian Fen or Zhao Feiyan.

sentences.zh: 而後世觀其若此，深懷酸毒之戒也。

translations.literal: Later generations observing them thus, deeply cherish sour-poison warnings.
translations.idiomatic: Later ages looked back with bitter lessons etched in memory.

sentences.zh: 至於魏文，遂發一概之詔，可謂有識之爽言，非帝者之宏議。〉

translations.literal: As for Wei Wen, thereupon issued blanket edict—can be called refreshing words with insight, not grand discussion of emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei then issued a sweeping prohibition—sound caution for a private gentleman, but hardly the balanced judgment expected of a sovereign."

sentences.zh: 庚子，立皇后郭氏。

translations.literal: Gengzi, established Empress Guo.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day Lady Guo was invested as empress.

sentences.zh: 賜天下男子爵人二級；

translations.literal: Bestowed on realm's men noble rank two grades each;
translations.idiomatic: Every adult male in the realm received two steps of noble rank;

sentences.zh: 鰥寡篤癃及貧不能自存者賜穀。

translations.literal: Widowers, widows, seriously infirm and poor unable self preserve were granted grain.
translations.idiomatic: widowers, widows, the severely disabled, and the destitute were given grain relief.

sentences.zh: 是月，孫權復叛。

translations.literal: This month, Sun Quan again rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: That month Sun Quan rebelled again.

sentences.zh: 復郢州爲荊州。

translations.literal: Restored Ying Province to be Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Ying province was merged back into Jing province.

sentences.zh: 帝自許昌南征，諸軍兵並進，權臨江拒守。

translations.literal: The Emperor from Xuchang campaigned south, various army soldiers advanced together; Quan along river resisted and guarded.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor marched south from Xuchang with converging columns while Sun Quan held the Yangzi line.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛丑，行幸宛。

translations.literal: Eleventh month Xinchou, progressed to favor Wan.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou day in the eleventh month he traveled to Wan.

sentences.zh: 庚申晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: Last day Gengshen, there was solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the month (gengshen) there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 是歲，穿靈芝池。

translations.literal: This year, dug Lingzhi Pond.
translations.idiomatic: That year work began on the Lingzhi Pond.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，有鵜鶘鳥集靈芝池，詔曰：「此詩人所謂污澤也。

translations.literal: Summer fifth month, there were pelican birds gathered at Lingzhi Pond; edict said: "This is what poets call the foul marsh.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer pelicans gathered on Lingzhi Pond; an edict observed, "The Odes call such birds creatures of fouled marshes.

sentences.zh: 曹詩『刺恭公遠君子而近小人』，今豈有賢智之士處于下位乎？

translations.literal: Cao's poem 'satirizes Duke Gong for distant gentlemen and near petty men'—now how can there be worthy wise gentlemen dwelling in lower positions?
translations.idiomatic: The poem of Cao satirizes Duke Gong for shunning gentlemen and favoring petty men—are wise worthies now languishing in low posts?

sentences.zh: 否則斯鳥何爲而至？

translations.literal: Otherwise why did this bird come?
translations.idiomatic: If not, why would such birds appear?

sentences.zh: 其博舉天下儁德茂才、獨行君子，以荅曹人之刺。」

translations.literal: Broadly raise all-under-heaven outstanding virtue flourishing talent, solitary-practice gentlemen, to answer Cao people's satire."
translations.idiomatic: Let every commandery recommend men of brilliant virtue, unusual integrity, and solitary excellence to answer the lesson of Cao's ode."

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：辛酉，有司奏造二廟，立太皇帝廟，大長秋特進侯與高祖合祭，親盡以次毀；

translations.literal: Wei Book says: On Xinyou, responsible offices memorialized constructing two temples, establishing Grand Emperor temple; Grand Coachman specially advanced marquis with Gaozu combined sacrifice; kin exhausted by degrees destroyed;
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book notes that on the xinyou day officials proposed building twin shrines: one for the Grand Emperor—sharing offerings with Gaozu until the generational tie lapsed—then to be dismantled in turn;

sentences.zh: 特立武皇帝廟，四時享祀，爲魏太祖，萬載不毀也。〉

translations.literal: singly established Martial Emperor temple, four seasons enjoy sacrifice, as Wei Taizu, myriad ages not destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: a separate temple enshrined Martial Emperor as Wei Founder with quarterly sacrifices, never to be torn down."

sentences.zh: 五年春正月，初令謀反大逆乃得相告，其餘皆勿聽治；

translations.literal: Fifth year spring first month, first ordinance: plotting rebellion great treason only then permitted mutually inform; all others do not listen or prosecute;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the fifth year he first allowed informants only for capital treason; all other accusations were rejected;

sentences.zh: 敢妄相告，以其罪罪之。

translations.literal: Dare falsely mutually inform—by their crime punish them.
translations.idiomatic: false denouncers would themselves suffer the penalty they sought.

sentences.zh: 三月，行自許昌還洛陽宮。

translations.literal: Third month, progressed from Xuchang returning to Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he returned from Xuchang to Luoyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，立太學，制五經課試之法，置春秋穀梁博士。

translations.literal: Summer fourth month, established Imperial University, regulated Five Classics examination/testing methods, established Spring and Autumn Guliang erudite.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he founded the Imperial University, set examinations on the Five Classics, and appointed an erudite for the Guliang commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 五月，有司以公卿朝朔望日，因奏疑事，聽斷大政，論辨得失。

translations.literal: Fifth month, responsible offices by dukes and ministers court new and full moon days, thereby memorializing doubtful affairs, hearing and deciding great policies, debating right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month officials arranged for the high ministers to attend court on the first and fifteenth of each month to raise doubtful cases, deliberate major policy, and debate merits and faults.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，行東巡，幸許昌宮。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, progressed east tour, favored Xuchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn he toured east and lodged at Xuchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 八月，爲水軍，親御龍舟，循蔡、頴，浮淮，幸壽春。

translations.literal: Eighth month, made naval army, personally piloted dragon boat, followed Cai and Ying, floated Huai, favored Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he raised a river fleet, boarded the imperial dragon barge, sailed the Cai and Ying rivers onto the Huai, and visited Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 揚州界將吏士民，犯五歲刑已下，皆原除之。

translations.literal: Yang Province boundary generals clerks soldiers people, committing five-year punishments and below, all pardoned removed.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout Yang province every officer, soldier, or commoner sentenced to five years or less was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 九月，遂至廣陵，赦青、徐二州，改易諸將守。

translations.literal: Ninth month, thereupon reached Guangling, pardoned Qing and Xu two provinces, changed various generals and guardians.
translations.idiomatic: In September he reached Guangling, issued amnesties for Qing and Xu provinces, and rotated the regional commanders.

sentences.zh: 冬十月乙卯，太白晝見。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month Yimao, Taibai seen in daytime.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao day in the tenth month Venus appeared in daylight.

sentences.zh: 行還許昌宮。

translations.literal: Progressed returning to Xuchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Xuchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載癸酉詔曰：「近之不綏，何遠之懷？

translations.literal: Wei Book carries Guiyou edict saying: "Near not pacified, how far cherish?
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book preserves a guiyou day edict: "If those nearby lack peace, how can we embrace what lies far off?

sentences.zh: 今事多而民少，上下相弊以文法，百姓無所措其手足。

translations.literal: Now affairs many but people few, above and below mutually harm by documentary law; hundred families nowhere place their hands and feet.
translations.idiomatic: Today business overwhelms a shrinking populace; officials and people tie each other in legal knots until commoners cannot move hand or foot.

sentences.zh: 昔泰山之哭者，以爲苛政甚於猛虎，吾備儒者之風，服聖人之遺教，豈可以目翫其辭，行違其誡者哉？

translations.literal: Formerly Taishan's weeper thought harsh government worse than fierce tiger; I prepare Ru scholar's wind, submit to sage's transmitted teaching—how can eye play with their phrases, walk violate their warnings?
translations.idiomatic: The mourner at Mount Tai thought cruel government fiercer than tigers—I profess Confucian teaching and obey the sages; shall I mouth their words while acting against their warning?

sentences.zh: 廣議輕刑，以惠百姓。」〉

translations.literal: Broadly deliberate light punishments, to benefit hundred families."
translations.idiomatic: Let every minister propose lighter sentences to benefit the people."

sentences.zh: 十一月庚寅，以冀州饑，遣使者開倉廩振之。

translations.literal: Eleventh month Gengyin, because Ji Province hunger, dispatched envoys opening granaries to relieve them.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengyin day in the eleventh month, owing to famine in Ji province, envoys opened the granaries for relief.

sentences.zh: 戊申晦，日有食之。

translations.literal: Last day Wushen, there was solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the month (wushen) there was a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 十二月，詔曰：「先王制禮，所以昭孝事祖，大則郊社，其次宗廟，三辰五行，名山大川，非此族也，不在祀典。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, edict said: "Former kings regulated ritual, thereby clarifying filial service to ancestors—great then suburban and soil sacrifices; next ancestral temples; three luminaries five phases, famous mountains great rivers—not this category, not in sacrifice canon.
translations.idiomatic: A December edict read: "Ancient kings framed ritual to show filial devotion to ancestors—chiefly the suburban rites to Heaven and earth, next the ancestral temples, then the luminaries, elements, famous peaks, and great rivers; nothing outside this list belongs in the canon of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 叔世衰亂，崇信巫史，至乃宮殿之內，戶牖之間，無不沃酹，甚矣其惑也。

translations.literal: Later generation decline chaos, exalted trusted shamans scribes—reaching to palace halls inside, doors windows between, none not poured libations—extreme indeed their delusion.
translations.idiomatic: Degenerate ages exalted shamans until libations splashed even inside palace chambers—such folly ran rampant.

sentences.zh: 自今，其敢設非祀之祭，巫祝之言，皆以執左道論，著于令典。

translations.literal: From now, dare establish non-canon sacrifices, shaman invocator speeches—all treated by practicing left-path doctrine, recorded in ordinance canon.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth anyone who stages illicit sacrifices or spreads shamanic prophecy shall be prosecuted as practicing heterodox arts and the prohibition shall be codified in written law.

sentences.zh: 」是歲穿天淵池。

translations.literal: " This year dug Tianyuan Pond.
translations.idiomatic: That same year saw excavation of the Tianyuan Pond.

sentences.zh: 六年春二月，遣使者循行許昌以東盡沛郡，問民所疾苦，貧者振貸之。

translations.literal: Sixth year spring second month, dispatched envoys touring east of Xuchang to reach Pei commandery, asking people what bitter ailments; poor ones relieved lent them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of spring of the sixth year inspectors toured from Xuchang east through Pei commandery, inquiring after hardships and granting grain loans to the poor.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏略》載詔曰：「昔軒轅建四面之號，周武稱『予有亂臣十人』，斯蓋先聖所以體國君民，亮成天工，多賢爲貴也。

translations.literal: Wei Summary carries edict saying: "Formerly Xuanyuan established four-side titles; Zhou Wu called 'I have disorder ministers ten persons'—this covers former sages thereby embodying state ruling people, bright completing heavenly work, many worthies as noble.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Summary preserves an edict: "The Yellow Emperor posted advisers on four sides; King Wu spoke of ten ministers who could cure chaos—because sage rulers cherish worthy ministers when ordering state and heaven's task alike.

sentences.zh: 今內有公卿以鎮京師，外設牧伯以監四方，至於元戎出征，則軍中宜有柱石之賢帥，輜重所在，又宜有鎮守之重臣，然後車駕可以周行天下，無內外之慮。

translations.literal: Now inside have dukes and ministers to guard capital city; outside establish shepherds and elders to supervise four quarters—as for commander-in-chief going campaign, then army center ought have pillar-stone worthy commander; baggage trains located place, again ought have guarding heavy ministers—then afterward imperial carriage can circle journey all-under-heaven, without internal-external worries.
translations.idiomatic: At court ministers stabilize Luoyang; in the regions governors watch the corners—when the supreme commander campaigns there must be stalwart generals in the field and trustworthy ministers guarding supply lines; only then can the emperor journey safely without dread inside or out.

sentences.zh: 吾今當征賊，欲守之積年。

translations.literal: I now about to campaign rebels, wish guard them accumulated years.
translations.idiomatic: I am about to strike the rebels and expect the duty to last several years.

sentences.zh: 其以尚書令潁鄉侯陳羣爲鎮軍大將軍，尚書僕射西鄉侯司馬懿爲撫軍大將軍。

translations.literal: Let Supervisor of the Secretariat Yingxiang Marquis Chen Qun be General Who Guards the Army; Deputy Director of the Secretariat Xixiang Marquis Sima Yi be General Who Pacifies the Army.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Qun, Marquis of Yingxiang, is named General Who Guards the Army, and Sima Yi, Marquis of Xixiang, General Who Pacifies the Army.

sentences.zh: 若吾臨江授諸將方略，則撫軍當留許昌，督後諸軍，錄後臺文書事；

translations.literal: If I along river grant generals plans, then Pacify Army should remain Xuchang, supervise rear various armies, record rear platform document affairs;
translations.idiomatic: If I take the front line to brief the generals, the Pacification general stays in Xuchang to coordinate rear echelons and handle secretariat paperwork;

sentences.zh: 鎮軍隨車駕，當董督衆軍，錄行尚書事；

translations.literal: Guard Army follows imperial carriage, should superintend oversee host of armies, record traveling Supervisor of Secretariat affairs;
translations.idiomatic: the general who guards the army escorts the throne, commands the host, and holds traveling authority as head of the secretariat;

sentences.zh: 皆假節鼓吹，給中軍兵騎六百人。

translations.literal: all lent credential drum-blow, supply center army soldiers cavalry six hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: each receives the credential, musicians, and six hundred guards from the central army.

sentences.zh: 吾欲去江數里，築宮室，往來其中，見賊可擊之形，便出奇兵擊之；

translations.literal: I wish go several li from river, build palace rooms, go-come within them, see enemy can strike form, then issue strange troops strike them;
translations.idiomatic: I will build a redoubt a few li from the river, move between it and the camp, and when the enemy offers a target I will sally with picked troops;

translations.idiomatic: if no opening appears I will exercise the six armies on hunt maneuvers and feast the troops."

sentences.zh: 三月，行幸召陵，通討虜渠。

translations.literal: Third month, progressed favor Shaoling, opened Taolu canal.
translations.idiomatic: In March he visited Shaoling and reopened the Taolu canal.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，還許昌宮。

translations.literal: Yisi, returned Xuchang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the yisi day he returned to Xuchang Palace.

sentences.zh: 并州刺史梁習討鮮卑軻比能，大破之。

translations.literal: Bing Province Inspector Liang Xi campaigned against Xianbei Ke Bineng, greatly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Xi, inspector of Bing province, attacked the Xianbei chief Kebineng and routed him.

sentences.zh: 辛未，帝爲舟師東征。

translations.literal: Xinwei, Emperor made naval army east campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinwei day the emperor led the river fleet east.

sentences.zh: 五月戊申，幸譙。

translations.literal: Fifth month Wushen, favored Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: On the wushen day in the fifth month he visited Qiao.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，熒惑入太微。

translations.literal: Renxu, Sparkling Deluder entered Supreme Subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: On the renxu day Mars entered the Supreme Palace enclosure.

sentences.zh: 六月，利成郡兵蔡方等以郡反，殺太守徐質。

translations.literal: Sixth month, Licheng commandery soldiers Cai Fang and others by commandery rebelled, killed Grand Administrator Xu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Licheng troops under Cai Fang rebelled and murdered Prefect Xu Zhi.

sentences.zh: 遣屯騎校尉任福、步兵校尉段昭與青州刺史討平之；

translations.literal: Dispatched Colonel of Garrison Cavalry Ren Fu, Colonel of Foot Soldiers Duan Zhao with Qing Province Inspector campaigned pacified them;
translations.idiomatic: Colonel Ren Fu of the garrison cavalry, Colonel Duan Zhao of the infantry, and the inspector of Qing province were sent to crush the rising;

sentences.zh: 其見脅略及亡命者，皆赦其罪。

translations.literal: Those seen coerced plundered and fugitive death—all pardon their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: those coerced into joining or driven into outlawry received amnesty.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，立皇子鑒爲東武陽王。

translations.literal: Autumn seventh month, established Imperial Son Jian as Prince of Dongwuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of autumn Prince Jian was named Prince of Dongwuyang.

sentences.zh: 八月，帝遂以舟師自譙循渦入淮，從陸道幸徐。

translations.literal: Eighth month, Emperor thereupon by naval army from Qiao followed Wo entered Huai, from land road favored Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In August the emperor led the fleet from Qiao up the Wo River into the Huai, then went overland to Xu.

sentences.zh: 九月，築東巡臺。

translations.literal: Ninth month, built East Tour Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In September he built the eastern inspection terrace.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，行幸廣陵故城，臨江觀兵，戎卒十餘萬，旌旗數百里。

translations.literal: Winter tenth month, progressed favored Guangling old city, overlooking river viewing troops—campaign soldiers over hundred thousand, banners several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he toured old Guangling, reviewed more than a hundred thousand troops along the river, with banners stretching for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》載帝於馬上爲詩曰：「觀兵臨江水，水流何湯湯！

translations.literal: Wei Book carries Emperor on horse composed poem saying: "View troops overlooking river water—water flow how surging surging!
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book quotes him composing on horseback: "I review the host beside the river—see how the current rolls!

sentences.zh: 戈矛成山林，玄甲曜日光。

translations.literal: Halberds spears become mountain forest; black armor dazzle sun light.
translations.idiomatic: Halberds rise like a forest; black lacquer armor flashes in the sun.

sentences.zh: 猛將懷暴怒，膽氣正從橫。

translations.literal: Fierce generals cherish violent rage; gall spirit just traverses horizontal.
translations.idiomatic: Fierce generals smolder with wrath; valor courses free through every rank.

sentences.zh: 誰云江水廣，一葦可以航，不戰屈敵虜，戢兵稱賢良。

translations.literal: Who says river water wide—one reed can navigate; not battle bend enemy captives—sheath weapons called worthy good.
translations.idiomatic: Who calls this river too wide? A reed could ferry us—better still to win without battle, sheathe swords, and pass as sages.

sentences.zh: 古公宅岐邑，實始翦殷商。

translations.literal: Ancient Duke dwelt Qi town—truly began trim Yin Shang.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient lord built at Qishan and began the undoing of Yin.

sentences.zh: 孟獻營虎牢，鄭人懼稽顙。

translations.literal: Meng Xian camped Hulao—Zheng people feared knock forehead.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Xian fortified Hulao until Zheng trembled and pressed brow to ground.

sentences.zh: 充國務耕殖，先零自破亡。

translations.literal: Chongguo devoted agriculture colonization—Xianling self broke perished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chongguo farmed the frontier until the Xianling tribes collapsed of themselves.

sentences.zh: 興農淮泗間，築室都徐方。

translations.literal: Raise agriculture Huai Si between—build houses capital Xu region.
translations.idiomatic: Let us till the lands between Huai and Si, raise walls, and make Xu our base.

sentences.zh: 量宜運權略，六軍咸恱康；

translations.literal: Measure fit transport stratagem—six armies all joyful health;
translations.idiomatic: Fit strategy to circumstance—then the six armies thrive in peace;

translations.idiomatic: unlike the Eastern Mountain ode with its endless ache of longing."

sentences.zh: 是歲大寒，水道冰，舟不得入江，乃引還。

translations.literal: This year great cold—water routes ice—boats could not enter river—thereupon led return.
translations.idiomatic: That winter bit deep; rivers froze and the fleet could not reach the Yangzi, so he withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十一月，東武陽王鑒薨。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, Prince of Dongwuyang Jian died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Prince Jian of Dongwuyang died.

sentences.zh: 十二月，行自譙過梁，遣使以太牢祀故漢太尉橋玄。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, progressed from Qiao passing Liang, dispatched envoy with grand beast sacrifice former Han Grand Commandant Qiao Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In December he traveled from Qiao through Liang and sent envoys with the grand sacrifice to honor the late Han Grand Commandant Qiao Xuan.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月，將幸許昌，許昌城南門無故自崩，帝心惡之，遂不入。

translations.literal: Seventh year spring first month, about to favor Xuchang—Xuchang city south gate without cause self collapsed—Emperor heart loathed it—thereupon did not enter.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring of the seventh year he meant to visit Xuchang, but the south gate collapsed without cause; taking it as an ill omen he turned back.

sentences.zh: 壬子，行還洛陽宮。

translations.literal: Renzi, progressed returned Luoyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the renzi day he returned to Luoyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 三月，築九華臺。

translations.literal: Third month, built Nine Splendor Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In March he built the Nine Splendors Terrace.

sentences.zh: 夏五月丙辰，帝疾篤，召中軍大將軍曹真、鎮軍大將軍陳羣、征東大將軍曹休、撫軍大將軍司馬宣王，並受遺詔輔嗣主。

translations.literal: Summer fifth month Bingchen, Emperor illness severe—summoned Central Army Grand General Cao Zhen, Guard Army Grand General Chen Qun, East Campaign Grand General Cao Xiu, Pacify Army Grand General Sima Xuanwang—all received testament edict assisting heir lord.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingchen day in the fifth month of summer, gravely ill, he summoned Cao Zhen, Chen Qun, Cao Xiu, and Sima Yi and entrusted them by testament to guide his heir.

sentences.zh: 遣後宮淑媛、昭儀已下歸其家。

translations.literal: Dispatched rear palace Shuyuan, Zhaoyi and below return their homes.
translations.idiomatic: Concubines ranked gentle ladies and below were sent home to their families.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，帝崩于嘉福殿，時年四十。

translations.literal: Dingsi, Emperor collapsed at Jiafu Hall, age then forty.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingsi day he died in Jiafu Hall at the age of forty.

sentences.zh: 〈《魏書》曰：殯於崇華前殿。〉

translations.literal: Wei Book says: Laying out at Chonghua Front Hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei Book states that his bier rested in the front hall of Chonghua."

sentences.zh: 六月戊寅，葬首陽陵。

translations.literal: Sixth month Wuyin, buried Shouyang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuyin day in the sixth month he was buried at Shouyang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 自殯及葬，皆以終制從事。

translations.literal: From laying out to burial, all by final regulations conducted affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From lying in state to interment every rite followed his own austere "final instructions."

sentences.zh: 〈《魏氏春秋》曰：明帝將送葬，曹真、陳羣、王朗等以暑熱固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: Wei Family Spring and Autumn says: Ming Di was about to escort burial—Cao Zhen, Chen Qun, Wang Lang etc. by summer heat firmly remonstrated—then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei shi chunqiu notes that Emperor Ming meant to join the funeral train but Cao Zhen, Chen Qun, Wang Lang, and others dissuaded him in the sweltering heat—so he desisted.

sentences.zh: 孫盛曰：夫窀穸之事，孝子之極痛也，人倫之道，於斯莫重。

translations.literal: Sun Sheng says: As for burial vault affairs—filial son's utmost pain; human relations way—here nothing heavier.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sheng remarks that laying a parent to rest is the filial son's sharpest grief—nothing weightier in human duty.

sentences.zh: 故天子七月而葬，同軌畢至。

translations.literal: Therefore Son of Heaven seventh month then bury—same track all arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the emperor waits seven months for burial so every carriage track may converge.

sentences.zh: 夫以義感之情，猶盡臨隧之哀，況乎天性發中，敦禮者重之哉！

translations.literal: By righteousness-moved feelings—still exhaust overseeing tunnel grief—how much more heavenly nature issuing center—those who esteem ritual value it!
translations.idiomatic: Even ritual bonds demand the full grief at the grave—how much more the bond of nature for those who prize propriety!

sentences.zh: 魏氏之德，仍世不基矣。

translations.literal: Wei clan's virtue—still generations not foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Such thin virtue ill suits lasting foundations for the house of Wei.

sentences.zh: 昔華元厚葬，君子以爲棄君於惡，羣等之諫，棄孰甚焉！

translations.literal: Formerly Hua Yuan thick burial—gentleman thought abandoned lord in evil—Qun etc.'s remonstrance—abandonance which more extreme!
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Hua Yuan gave a lavish funeral; the nobles read it as abandoning his lord to wrong—what greater betrayal than Chen Qun's counsel to stay away?

sentences.zh: 鄄城侯植爲誄曰：「惟黃初七年五月七日，大行皇帝崩，嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Marquis of Juancheng Zhi composed a dirge saying: "Only Huangchu seventh year fifth month seventh day, the Grand Procession Emperor collapsed—alas, how bitter is our grief!
translations.idiomatic: The Marquis of Juancheng, Cao Zhi, composed a dirge: "On the seventh day of the fifth month of Huangchu seven (226 CE) the late emperor passed away—alas, the sorrow!"

sentences.zh: 于時天震地駭，崩山隕霜，陽精薄景，五緯錯行，百姓呼嗟，萬國悲悼，若喪考妣，恩過墓唐，擗踊郊野，仰想穹蒼，僉曰何辜，早世殞喪，嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Then Heaven quaked and Earth was shaken; mountains split and frost fell; the sun's essence thinned its glory; the five planetary traces ran awry; the hundred surnames cried aloud; the myriad regions mourned—as mourning father and mother; kindness surpassed tomb-site Tang; beating breasts and stamping in the suburban wilds; looking up pondering deep azure—all said what guilt—early age perished loss—alas, how bitter is our grief!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven trembled and earth reeled; peaks shattered and frost fell; the sun's fire dimmed; the five planets left their tracks; people wailed and every polity grieved as for lost parents; kindness deeper than at Tang's tomb; mourners beat their breasts in the outer suburbs and scanned the sky—why must guilt strike him who died before his time? Alas, the sorrow!"

sentences.zh: 悲夫大行，忽焉光滅，永棄萬國，雲往雨絕。

translations.literal: Alas for Grand Procession—suddenly radiance extinguished; forever cast off from myriad regions; clouds gone rain cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Alas for the departed sovereign—his light snuffed in an instant, forever lost to the realm; clouds have fled and the rains ceased."

sentences.zh: 承問荒忽，惛懵哽咽，袖鋒抽刃，歎自僵斃，追慕三良，甘心同穴。

translations.literal: Receiving tidings wild confused, dark dull choking—sleeve blade draw dagger—sigh self rigid death—long for Three Good Men—glad heart same cave.
translations.idiomatic: When the news reached me I reeled in confusion, voice choked—I would have drawn steel and struck myself down; I envied the three Good Men who followed Duke Mu into death and wished to share one tomb."

sentences.zh: 感惟南風，惟以鬱滯，終於偕沒，指景自誓。

translations.literal: Moved only south wind—only thereby pent stagnant—in end together perish—point shadow self swear.
translations.idiomatic: The south wind stirs grief still pent within us—we shall perish together; I swear by the moving sun."

sentences.zh: 考諸先記，尋之哲言，生若浮寄，惟德可論，朝聞夕逝，孔志所存。

translations.literal: Examine various former records—trace them sage words—life like floating lodging—only virtue can be discussed—dawn hear dusk depart—Kong resolve stored.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient texts and wise men taught that life is fleeting lodging and only virtue endures; "hear the Way at dawn, die content at dusk"—such was Confucius's pledge."

sentences.zh: 皇雖一沒，天祿永延，何以述德？

translations.literal: Sovereign though once gone—Heaven salary forever extended—how thereby narrate virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Though he has passed in one stroke, Heaven's blessing flows onward—how shall we proclaim his merit?"

sentences.zh: 表之素旃。

translations.literal: Display them plain white banners.
translations.idiomatic: We inscribe it on the white funeral banner."

sentences.zh: 何以詠功？

translations.literal: How thereby chant merit?
translations.idiomatic: How shall we sing his achievements?"

sentences.zh: 宣之管絃。

translations.literal: Proclaim them pipes strings.
translations.idiomatic: Let pipes and strings carry them abroad."

sentences.zh: 乃作誄曰：皓皓太素，兩儀始分，中和產物，肈有人倫，爰曁三皇，寔秉道真，降逮五帝，繼以懿純，三代製作，踵武立勳。

translations.literal: Thus composing dirge says: Bright bright Great Simplicity—two powers first divided—center harmony produced creatures—thereupon human relations—then reaching Three August Ones—truly grasped Way true—descending reaching Five Thearchs—in succession with pure grace—Three Ages fashioned institutions—heel-print martial raised merit.
translations.idiomatic: The dirge continues: "Bright primal purity split into yin and yang and yielded the human order; the Three Sovereigns grasped the true Dao, the Five Thearchs followed in unstained line, and the Three Dynasties built institutions and trod the path of merit."

sentences.zh: 季嗣不維，網漏于秦，崩樂滅學，儒坑禮焚，二世而殲，漢氏乃因，弗求古訓，嬴政是遵，王綱帝典，闃爾無聞。

translations.literal: Later heirs not bind—net leaked under Qin—collapse music destroy learning—Ru buried ritual burned—Second Generation then destroyed—Han clan thereupon continued—not seeking ancient instructions—Ying Zheng this followed—kingly cord imperial canon—silent indeed unheard.
translations.idiomatic: Successors failed their bond; Qin's net tore—music fell and learning died, Confucians were buried and ritual texts burned; Er Shi fell within two reigns. Han arose yet spurned antique teaching and copied the First Emperor until royal norms seemed lost in silence."

sentences.zh: 末光幽昧，道究運遷，乾坤迴歷，簡聖授賢，乃眷大行，屬以黎元。

translations.literal: Last gleam dark dim—Way exhausted fortune shift—Qian Kun circuit rounds—select sage grant worthy—then favor Grand Procession—entrust with black-haired masses.
translations.idiomatic: Twilight deepened until fortune shifted; heaven and earth rolled through cycles until the canon chose sages—and then He turned to the late emperor and entrusted him with the black-haired masses."

sentences.zh: 龍飛啟祚，合契上玄，五行定紀，改號革年，明明赫赫，受命于天。

translations.literal: Dragon fly open fortune—combine tally Upper Dark—Five Phases fix records—change designation reform year—bright bright blazing blazing—receive mandate from Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The dragon throne rose, cosmic tallies aligned with High Heaven, the Five Agents received their stations, reign titles and years were renewed—radiant and august, he bore Heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 仁風偃物，德以禮宣；

translations.literal: Humane wind lay things low—virtue by ritual proclaimed;
translations.idiomatic: His humane breezes bowed all creation; his power moved through ritual;

sentences.zh: 祥惟聖質，嶷在幼妍。

translations.literal: Auspicious only sage substance—towering in youth grace.
translations.idiomatic: augury marked his sacred nature, steadfast even in childhood grace.

sentences.zh: 庻幾六典，學不過庭，潛心無罔，亢志青冥。

translations.literal: Almost Six Canons—learning not passing courtyard—sink heart without deceit—raise resolve blue-dark.
translations.idiomatic: He aspired to the Six Canons, studied within his courtyard, pondered without guile, and raised his purpose toward the empyrean.

sentences.zh: 才秀藻朗，如玉之瑩，聽察無嚮，瞻覩未形。

translations.literal: Talent splendid polish bright—like jade's luster—hearing examining without direction—gazing seeing unformed.
translations.idiomatic: Talent shone clear as polished jade; his hearing needed no prompting, his sight pierced what had not yet taken shape.

sentences.zh: 其剛如金，其貞如瓊，如氷之絜，如砥之平。

translations.literal: His hardness like gold—his constancy like fine jade—like ice's purity—like whetstone's level.
translations.idiomatic: He was hard as metal, constant as jade, pure as ice, level as a whetstone.

sentences.zh: 爵公無私，戮違無輕，心鏡萬機，攬照下情。

translations.literal: Ennobling dukes without selfishness—punishing rebels without lightness—heart mirrors myriad mechanisms—gather shine lower feelings.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed without favoritism and punished rebels without laxity; his mind mirrored every policy and illumined the people's plight.

sentences.zh: 思良股肱，嘉昔伊呂，搜揚側陋，舉湯代禹；

translations.literal: Thought good thighs arms—praised former Yi Lü—search raise humble obscure—raise Tang replace Yu;
translations.idiomatic: He sought worthy limbs of state, praised Yi Yin and Lü Wang, searched humble lanes and raised men like Tang's ministers;

sentences.zh: 拔才巖穴，取士蓬戶，唯德是縈，弗拘禰祖。

translations.literal: Pull talent cave grottoes—take scholars brushwood doors—only virtue is bound—not constrain Mi Zu.
translations.idiomatic: he drew talent from mountain caves and brushwood gates, binding office to virtue alone without respect to pedigree.

sentences.zh: 宅土之表，道義是圖，弗營厥險，六合是虞。

translations.literal: Dwelling earth's surface—Way righteousness this plan—not fortify those perils—six unions this guard.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the nine provinces he sought righteousness, scorned mere terrain, and watched over the six directions.

sentences.zh: 齊契共遵，下以純民，恢折規矩，克紹前人。

translations.literal: Level tally together obey—below thereby pure people—expand break compass-square—able continue former men.
translations.idiomatic: All signed the covenant to guide the folk in simplicity, broadened the norms, and carried on the work of past kings.

sentences.zh: 科條品制，襃貶以因。

translations.literal: Statutes articles grades systems—praise blame thereby follow.
translations.idiomatic: Statutes and ranks framed praise and blame by precedent.

sentences.zh: 乘殷之輅，行夏之辰。

translations.literal: Ride Yin's chariot—practice Xia's calendar.
translations.idiomatic: He rode Yin-style chariots and kept Xia's calendar.

sentences.zh: 金根黃屋，翠葆龍鱗，紼冕崇麗，衡紞惟新，尊肅禮容，矚之若神。

translations.literal: Gold Root Yellow Canopy—emerald feather dragon scales—cord cap lofty splendid—cross-cord only new—revere solemn ritual bearing—gaze it like spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Gold-decked chariot and yellow canopy, kingfisher pennons and dragon scales on regalia; cords and crowns rose in splendor, hatstrings gleamed anew—his solemn ritual awe struck every eye like a god.

sentences.zh: 方牧妙舉，欽於恤民，虎將荷節，鎮彼四鄰；

translations.literal: Regional shepherds wonderful selections—revere at relieving people—tiger generals bearing credential—guard those four neighbors;
translations.idiomatic: Regional governors were wisely chosen and cherished the people; tiger generals bore credentials and pacified the marches;

sentences.zh: 朱旗所勦，九壤被震，疇克不若？

translations.literal: Red flags wherever strike—nine soils struck quake—who can not submit?
translations.idiomatic: Wherever crimson banners swept the nine regions trembled—who could refuse submission?

sentences.zh: 孰敢不臣？

translations.literal: Who dares not minister?
translations.idiomatic: Who dared withhold allegiance?

sentences.zh: 縣旌海表，萬里無塵。

translations.literal: Suspend banners sea beyond—ten thousand li without dust.
translations.idiomatic: Banners flew beyond the eastern sea and ten thousand li knew no raider's dust.

sentences.zh: 虜備凶徹，鳥殪江岷，權若涸魚，乾腊矯鱗，肅慎納貢，越裳效珍，條支絕域，侍子內賔。

translations.literal: Captive Bei fierce exhausted—birds destroyed Jiang Min—Quan like dried fish—dried flesh stiff scales—Sushen bring tribute—Yuechang present treasures—Tiaozhi cut-off region—hostage sons inner guests.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Bei's host was broken along the rivers; Sun Quan gasped like a fish on dry land; Sushen sent tribute, Yuechang offered jades, even far Tiaozhi sent hostages to court.

sentences.zh: 德儕先皇，功侔太古。

translations.literal: Virtue equal Former Emperor—merit match Grand Antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: His virtue matched the ancient sovereigns; his deeds rivaled high antiquity.

sentences.zh: 上靈降瑞，黃初叔祜：河龍洛龜，淩波游下；

translations.literal: Upper spirits descend auspicious—Huangchu secondary blessing: River Dragon Luo Tortoise—stride waves swim down;
translations.idiomatic: High Heaven sent omens and Huangchu knew felicity: dragons rose from the Yellow River and tortoises from the Luo, breasting the waves;

sentences.zh: 平鈞應繩，神鸞翔舞；

translations.literal: Level jun responds cord—divine luan soar dance;
translations.idiomatic: the measuring cord hung true and divine phoenixes wheeled in dance;

sentences.zh: 數莢階除，系風扇暑；

translations.literal: Repeated pods stair steps—tie wind fan summer;
translations.idiomatic: auspicious grain sprouted on the stairs; gentle winds turned aside the summer heat;

sentences.zh: 皓獸素禽，飛走郊野；

translations.literal: White beasts plain birds—fly run suburban wilds;
translations.idiomatic: white beasts and bright-plumed birds crossed the suburban preserves;

sentences.zh: 神鍾寶鼎，形自舊土；

translations.literal: Divine bell precious tripod—forms from old soil;
translations.idiomatic: spirit bells and bronze tripods took shape from native earth;

sentences.zh: 雲英甘露，瀸塗被宇；

translations.literal: Cloud essence sweet dew—moisten mud cover roof;
translations.idiomatic: sweet nectar washed the dust and bathed the palace roof;

sentences.zh: 靈芝冒沼，朱華陰渚。

translations.literal: Numinous fungus cover marsh—red flowers shade islet.
translations.idiomatic: magic fungus crowned the ponds and crimson flowers shaded the islets.

sentences.zh: 回回凱風，祁祁甘雨，稼穡豐登，我稷我黍。

translations.literal: Whirling triumphant wind—vast vast sweet rain—grain crops abundant rising—our millet our glutinous millet.
translations.idiomatic: Soft southern breezes brought abundant rains; grain stood thick—our wheat and millet flourished.

sentences.zh: 家佩惠君，戶蒙慈父。

translations.literal: Households wear gracious lord—doors receive kindly father.
translations.idiomatic: Every home cherished him as a gracious lord; every door knew him as a kindly father.

sentences.zh: 圖致太和，洽德全義。

translations.literal: Plan reach Grand Harmony—moisten virtue complete righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He aimed at supreme harmony and mingled virtue with perfect righteousness.

sentences.zh: 將登介山，先皇作儷。

translations.literal: About to ascend Jie Mountain—Former Emperor made mate.
translations.idiomatic: He prepared to climb Mount Jie as Shun once did, pairing ritual with the founder.

sentences.zh: 鐫石紀勳，兼錄衆瑞，方隆封禪，歸功天地，賔禮百靈，勳命視規，望祭四嶽，燎封奉柴，肅于南郊，宗祀上帝。

translations.literal: Carve stone record merit—also record crowd auspicious—about to elevate Feng Shan—return merit Heaven Earth—guest-ritual hundred spirits—merit mandate inspect regulation—gaze sacrifice Four Marchmounts—blaze seal offer firewood—solemn at southern suburb—ancestral sacrifice Supreme Lord.
translations.idiomatic: He carved stone to record deeds and gathered every omen; about to mount Feng and Shan he returned merit to Heaven and earth, feasted the hundred spirits, inspected ordinances, sacrificed to the Four Peaks, burned grain offerings at the suburban altar, and honored High God in the ancestral shrine.

sentences.zh: 三牲旣供，夏禘秋甞，元侯佐祭，獻璧奉璋。

translations.literal: Three victims already supplied—summer di autumn taste—chief marquises assist sacrifice—present jade disk offer jade tablet.
translations.idiomatic: Tripods steamed with three beasts; summer di and autumn chang rites brought chief marquises to assist, presenting disks and libation tablets.

sentences.zh: 鸞輿幽藹，龍旂太常，爰迄太廟，鍾鼓鍠鍠，頌德詠功，八佾鏘鏘。

translations.literal: Luan carriage dim mist—dragon pennant Grand Constant—thereupon reach Grand Temple—bells drums clang clang—praise virtue chant merit—eight rows clang clang.
translations.idiomatic: Phoenix carriages drifted in gloom; dragon banners flew from the Grand Constant guard; entering the Grand Temple bells and drums thundered while eight rows of dancers praised virtue and rehearsed his deeds.

sentences.zh: 皇祖旣饗，烈考來享，神具醉止，降茲福祥。

translations.literal: Imperial Grandfather already feast—Fiery Deceased comes enjoy—spirits all drunk stop—descend this blessing auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial ancestors received the feast; his father joined in joy—the spirits drank their fill and poured forth fortune.

sentences.zh: 天地震蕩，大行康之；

translations.literal: Heaven Earth shake surge—Grand Procession rested them;
translations.idiomatic: When heaven and earth convulsed, the late emperor brought peace;

sentences.zh: 三辰暗昧，大行光之；

translations.literal: Three luminaries dark dim—Grand Procession brightened them;
translations.idiomatic: when sun, moon, and stars grew dim, he lit them anew;

sentences.zh: 皇紘絕維，大行綱之；

translations.literal: Imperial cord cut rope—Grand Procession corded them;
translations.idiomatic: when the royal net snapped, he restrung it;

sentences.zh: 神器莫統，大行當之；

translations.literal: Divine vessel none unify—Grand Procession bore it;
translations.idiomatic: when the sacred regalia lacked a master, he took it up;

sentences.zh: 禮樂廢弛，大行張之；

translations.literal: Rite music abandoned slack—Grand Procession stretched them;
translations.idiomatic: when ritual and music collapsed, he stretched them taut;

sentences.zh: 仁義陸沈，大行揚之；

translations.literal: Benevolence righteousness sunk land—Grand Procession raised them;
translations.idiomatic: when humanity and justice sank from sight, he raised them high;

sentences.zh: 潛龍隱鳳，大行翔之；

translations.literal: Hidden dragon concealed phoenix—Grand Procession soared them;
translations.idiomatic: when dragons hid and phoenixes vanished, he gave them flight;

sentences.zh: 疏狄遐康，大行匡之。

translations.literal: Distant Di far Kang—Grand Procession corrected them.
translations.idiomatic: when distant Di tribes lacked peace, he set them right.

sentences.zh: 在位七載，元功仍舉，將永太和，絕迹三五，宜作物師，長爲神主，壽終金石，等筭東父，如何奄忽，摧身后土，俾我棾棾，靡瞻靡顧。

translations.literal: On throne seven years—prime merit still raised—about to eternal Grand Harmony—cut traces Three Five—should serve creation teacher—long as spirit lord—life end metal stone—equal reckon Eastern Father—how sudden abruptly—break body rear earth—cause me solitary solitary—none gaze none look.
translations.idiomatic: Seven years on the throne—great deeds piled toward lasting harmony, rivaling the Three Dynasties—fit to be maker of laws and everlasting lord, to live long as bronze stone like Dongfang Shuo—yet suddenly earth swallowed him, leaving us orphaned with nowhere to turn our eyes.

sentences.zh: 嗟嗟皇穹，胡寧忍務？

translations.literal: Alas alas august vault—how indeed endure task?
translations.idiomatic: O mighty Heaven—how could you bear this deed?

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas how bitter grief!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, the sorrow!

sentences.zh: 明監吉凶，體遠存亡，深垂典制，申之嗣皇。

translations.literal: Bright mirror auspicious inauspicious—embody far survival loss—deep suspend canon regulations—extend them heir emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-eyed toward fortune and fate, he gauged life and death from afar—his ordinances reach deep and instruct the heir.

sentences.zh: 聖上虔奉，是順是將，乃剏玄宇，基爲首陽，擬迹穀林，追堯慕唐，合山同陵，不樹不疆，塗車芻靈，珠玉靡藏。

translations.literal: Holy superior reverently uphold—this obey this lead—thereupon carve Dark Hall—foundation be Shouyang—trace footprints Grain Grove—pursue Yao admire Tang—join mountains same mound—not trees not borders—clay cart straw spirits—pearls jades none bury.

translations.idiomatic: Returning to my seat I laughed: "Once Yang Qing made Chunyu Yi throw away old prescriptions for secret cures—I urge General Deng to cast off stale tricks and learn the true essentials.

sentences.zh: 」一坐盡歡。

translations.literal: " Full seated all joy.
translations.idiomatic: The whole company roared approval.

sentences.zh: 夫事不可自謂己長，余少曉持複，自謂無對；

translations.literal: As for affairs cannot self-call self long—I youth understood wield paired—I self-called none match;
translations.idiomatic: One must never boast one's skill; young, I mastered twin halberds and thought none could touch me;

sentences.zh: 俗名雙戟爲坐鐵室，鑲楯爲蔽木戶；

translations.literal: Common name paired ji as sit iron chamber—inlaid shield as screen wood door;
translations.idiomatic: folk nicknamed paired ji "iron chamber" and inlaid shields "wooden shutters";

sentences.zh: 後從陳國袁敏學，以單攻複，每爲若神，對家不知所出，先曰若逢敏於狹路，直決耳！

translations.literal: Later followed Chen state Yuan Min learned—use single attack paired—every act like spirit—opponent family know not where emerge—first said if meet Min at narrow road—straight decide ear!
translations.idiomatic: later Chen Yuan Min taught me to pit single halberd against twin until my moves seemed sorcerous—foes saw no opening—and he warned that meeting Min on a narrow path meant instant defeat!

sentences.zh: 余於他戲弄之事少所喜，唯彈棊略盡其巧，少爲之賦。

translations.literal: I about other play jest matters little liked—only stone chess somewhat exhausted its subtlety—young for it composed rhapsody.
translations.idiomatic: Other games bored me—only ball-board chess drew out every subtlety, and I wrote a youthful rhapsody on it.

sentences.zh: 昔京師先工有馬合鄉侯、東方安世、張公子，常恨不得與彼數子者對。

translations.literal: Formerly capital former masters had Ma Hexiang Marquis—Dongfang Anshi—Zhang Gongzi—always regretted unable with those several masters match.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang once boasted masters such as the Marquis of Mahe township, Dongfang Anshi, and Lord Zhang—I always regretted missing a match with them.

sentences.zh: 上雅好詩書文籍，雖在軍旅，手不釋卷，每每定省從容，常言人少好學則思專，長則善忘，長大而能勤學者，唯吾與袁伯業耳。

translations.literal: Above refined loved poetry books writings—even in military hosts—hand not release scroll—often settled leisure—always said people youth good study then thought focused—grown then apt forget—grown large yet able diligent study—only I and Yuan Boye ears.
translations.idiomatic: My father loved belles-lettres even on campaign—never without a scroll—and often mused that youth loves study with single mind yet grown men forget; among adults who still labor at books only I and Yuan Boye remain.

sentences.zh: 余是以少誦詩、論，及長而備歷五經、四部，史、漢、諸子百家之言，靡不畢覽。

translations.literal: I thereby youth recited Poetry Analects—reaching grown then fully traversed Five Classics Four Sections—Histories Han hundred schools speech—none not completed perused.
translations.idiomatic: Thus I memorized the Odes and Analects as a boy and later surveyed the Five Classics, four bibliographic divisions, the histories, Hanshu, and every philosopher.

sentences.zh: 《博物志》曰：帝善彈棊，能用手巾角。

translations.literal: Treatise on Broad Things of Antiquity says: Emperor good stone chess—able use handkerchief corner.
translations.idiomatic: The Bowuzhi notes that the emperor excelled at ball-board chess and could flick pieces with his kerchief corner.

sentences.zh: 時有一書生，又能低頭以所冠著葛巾角撇棊。〉

translations.literal: At time one scholar-student—again able lower head with worn Ge kerchief corner flick chess.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar was seen bending his head to snap pieces with the hemp kerchief he wore.

sentences.zh: 若加之曠大之度，勵以公平之誠，邁志存道，克廣德心，則古之賢主，何遠之有哉！

translations.literal: If add to vast magnanimous measure—encourage by fairness sincerity—stride resolve preserve Way—able broaden virtue heart—then ancient worthy lords—what far have there!
translations.idiomatic: Had he joined those gifts with boundless tolerance, fairness, devotion to the Way, and ever-broadening virtue, how far would he stand from the sage rulers of old!
